Meanwhile cook the rice in a lidded pan with 300 ml of water: boil, cover, reduce to the lowest heat for 12 minutes, then rest off the heat.
Whisk the miso, mirin, soy sauce and sugar with 1 tbsp of water until smooth.
Turn the aubergine cut-side up, spread the miso glaze over the flesh and roast for 8 to 10 minutes more until sticky and bubbling at the edges.
Serve the aubergine on the rice with the cucumber, spring onion and sesame seeds.

recipes.title: Miso tofu and mushroom udon broth
recipes.blurb: A light, savoury miso broth with chunky udon, golden tofu, mushrooms and pak choi.
steps: Heat the vegetable oil in a saucepan over a medium-high heat and fry the tofu for 5 minutes, turning until golden on most sides. Remove and set aside.
In the same pan, fry the mushrooms and ginger for 4 minutes until lightly browned.
Add 700 ml of water, the crumbled stock cube, soy sauce and mirin and bring to a simmer.
Add the udon and pak choi and simmer for 3 minutes until the noodles are loose and hot.
Ladle a little broth into a cup, whisk in the miso until smooth and stir it back into the pan. Do not boil it again.
Divide into bowls, top with the tofu and spring onion and finish with the sesame oil.

recipes.title: Gochujang pork rice bowl
recipes.blurb: Sticky, spicy pork mince over rice with quick-pickled cucumber and crunchy carrot.
steps: Cook the rice in a lidded pan with 300 ml of water: boil, cover, reduce to the lowest heat for 12 minutes and rest off the heat.
Toss the cucumber with the rice vinegar and a pinch of the sugar and leave to pickle.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over a high heat and fry the pork, breaking it up, for 6 minutes until browned and any liquid has cooked off.
Add the garlic, ginger and half the spring onion for 1 minute, then stir in the gochujang, soy sauce, sugar and 3 tbsp of water. Cook for 2 to 3 minutes until sticky.
Spoon the pork over the rice with the cucumber and carrot. Drizzle with the sesame oil and scatter over the sesame seeds and remaining spring onion.

recipes.title: Veggie bibimbap with a fried egg
recipes.blurb: Rice topped with sesame spinach, carrots, mushrooms and a runny egg, finished with gochujang sauce.
steps: Cook the rice in a lidded pan with 300 ml of water: boil, cover, reduce to the lowest heat for 12 minutes and rest off the heat.
Stir the gochujang, sugar, 1 tsp of the sesame oil and 2 tbsp of water into a sauce.
Wilt the spinach in a hot pan for 1 minute, squeeze out the water and toss with 1 tsp of soy sauce, a little sesame oil, the garlic and the salt.
Fry the carrot in 1 tbsp of the vegetable oil for 3 minutes, then remove. Fry the mushrooms in the same pan with the remaining soy sauce for 5 minutes until golden.
Fry the eggs in the remaining oil over a medium-high heat for 2 to 3 minutes until the whites are crisp and the yolks runny.
Divide the rice between bowls, arrange the vegetables and cucumber on top and add an egg. Drizzle with the remaining sesame oil, scatter with sesame seeds and serve with the sauce to stir through.

recipes.title: Kimchi and crispy tofu fried rice
recipes.blurb: Tangy kimchi, golden tofu and gochujang-spiced rice in one wok. Hot, funky and fully vegan.
steps: Cook the rice in a lidded pan with 300 ml of water: boil, cover, reduce to the lowest heat for 12 minutes, then spread out on a tray to cool and dry.
Heat 2 tbsp of the oil in a wok over a high heat and fry the tofu for 6 to 7 minutes, tossing until crisp and golden. Remove and set aside.
Add the remaining oil, the spring onion whites, garlic and half the chilli and stir-fry for 30 seconds.
Add the kimchi and cook for 2 minutes, then add the gochujang and rice, tossing and pressing for 4 minutes until hot and lightly crisp.
Stir in the soy sauce and return the tofu. Serve with the sesame oil, sesame seeds, spring onion greens and remaining chilli.

recipes.title: Bulgogi-style beef rice bowl
recipes.blurb: Sweet, garlicky marinated beef seared hot and piled over rice with crisp lettuce and cucumber.
steps: Mix the soy sauce, sugar, half the sesame oil, garlic, ginger and grated apple in a bowl. Add the beef and marinate for at least 10 minutes while you cook the rice.
Cook the rice in a lidded pan with 300 ml of water: boil, cover, reduce to the lowest heat for 12 minutes and rest off the heat.
Heat the vegetable oil in a wok or large frying pan until very hot. Fry the beef in two batches for 2 minutes each, until caramelised at the edges.
Return all the beef with any marinade left in the bowl and bubble for 30 seconds.
Serve over the rice with lettuce leaves and cucumber, scattered with the spring onion and sesame seeds and drizzled with the remaining sesame oil.

recipes.title: Thai green chicken curry with green beans
recipes.blurb: Creamy coconut green curry with tender chicken thigh, courgette and green beans, finished with lime.
steps: Cook the rice in a lidded pan with 300 ml of water: boil, cover, reduce to the lowest heat for 12 minutes and rest off the heat.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over a medium-high heat. Fry the curry paste for 1 minute until fragrant, then add the chicken and stir for 3 minutes.
Pour in the coconut milk, fish sauce and sugar, bring to a gentle simmer and cook for 8 minutes.
Add the green beans and courgette and cook for 6 to 8 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and the vegetables are tender.
Squeeze in the juice of half the lime, taste and adjust. Serve with the rice, coriander and a wedge of the remaining lime.

recipes.title: Thai red sweet potato and spinach curry
recipes.blurb: Sweet potato and red pepper simmered in a fragrant coconut and red curry sauce with wilted spinach.

ingredients.name: Sweet potato
ingredients.prep: peeled and cut into 2 cm chunks

steps: Cook the rice in a lidded pan with 300 ml of water: boil, cover, reduce to the lowest heat for 12 minutes and rest off the heat.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over a medium heat and fry the curry paste for 1 minute.
Add the sweet potato and red pepper, stir to coat, then pour in the coconut milk, 100 ml of water, the soy sauce and the sugar.
Simmer gently for 15 to 18 minutes until the sweet potato is soft but holding its shape.
Stir in the spinach until wilted, then squeeze in half the lime juice. Serve with the rice, coriander and a lime wedge.

recipes.title: Prawn pad Thai with lime and peanuts
recipes.blurb: Wok-fried rice noodles with king prawns, egg and bean sprouts in a sweet-sour-salty sauce.
steps: Soak the noodles in just-boiled water for 6 to 8 minutes until pliable but firm, then drain.
Stir the fish sauce, vinegar, sugar, soy sauce and sriracha together in a small bowl until the sugar dissolves.
Heat half the oil in a wok over a high heat and fry the prawns for 2 minutes until pink, then remove.
Add the remaining oil, garlic and spring onion for 20 seconds. Push to one side, crack in the eggs and scramble for 30 seconds.
Add the noodles and sauce and toss for 2 to 3 minutes until the sauce is absorbed. Return the prawns, add the bean sprouts and toss for 1 minute.
Serve scattered with the peanuts and a lime wedge to squeeze over.

recipes.title: Thai-style pork with chilli, basil and green beans
recipes.blurb: A hot, salty-sweet pork stir-fry with plenty of chilli and basil, served over jasmine rice.
steps: Cook the rice in a lidded pan with 300 ml of water: boil, cover, reduce to the lowest heat for 12 minutes and rest off the heat.
Stir the oyster sauce, soy sauce, fish sauce, sugar and 2 tbsp of water together.
Heat the oil in a wok over a high heat. Add the chilli and garlic and stir for 15 seconds, then add the pork, breaking it up, and fry for 5 minutes until browned.
Add the green beans and sauce and stir-fry for 3 to 4 minutes until the beans are just tender and the sauce has reduced.
Take off the heat and stir through most of the basil. Serve over the rice with the remaining basil.

recipes.title: Peanut tofu and rice noodle bowl
recipes.blurb: Crisp tofu and crunchy vegetables with rice noodles in a creamy peanut, lime and chilli dressing.

ingredients.name: Firm tofu
ingredients.prep: cut into cubes and patted dry

steps: Soak the noodles in just-boiled water for 6 to 8 minutes until tender, then drain and rinse under cold water.
Whisk the peanut butter, soy sauce, juice of the lime, sriracha, ginger, garlic and 4 tbsp of warm water into a smooth dressing.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over a medium-high heat and fry the tofu for 8 minutes, turning, until crisp and golden.
Toss the noodles with the carrot, red pepper and most of the dressing.
Divide into bowls and top with the tofu, drizzle with the remaining dressing and scatter over the coriander and peanuts.

recipes.title: Lemongrass chicken noodle bowl
recipes.blurb: Fragrant lemongrass chicken over cool rice noodles, crunchy veg and herbs with a sharp lime dressing.
steps: Mix the lemongrass, half the garlic, 10 ml of the fish sauce and 5 g of the sugar through the chicken and leave to marinate while you prepare everything else.
Soak the noodles in just-boiled water for 6 to 8 minutes, drain and rinse under cold water.
Make the dressing by stirring the remaining fish sauce, garlic and sugar with the juice of 1½ limes, the chilli and 3 tbsp of water.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over a high heat and fry the chicken for 6 to 8 minutes until caramelised and cooked through.
Divide the noodles into bowls and top with the cucumber, carrot, herbs and chicken. Pour over the dressing and scatter with the peanuts and a wedge of the remaining lime.

recipes.title: Caramel ginger salmon with pak choi
recipes.blurb: Salmon glazed in a sticky caramel, ginger and fish sauce with steamed pak choi and rice.
steps: Cook the rice in a lidded pan with 300 ml of water: boil, cover, reduce to the lowest heat for 12 minutes and rest off the heat.

Melt the sugar with 1 tbsp of water in a small pan over a medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes until amber. Carefully add the fish sauce, 3 tbsp of water, the ginger, garlic and pepper and simmer for 2 minutes.
Heat the oil in a non-stick frying pan over a medium-high heat and sear the salmon for 3 minutes per side.
Pour in the caramel and spoon it over the fish for 1 to 2 minutes until sticky.
Meanwhile steam the pak choi in a covered pan with a splash of water for 3 minutes.
Serve the salmon over the rice with the pak choi, chilli, spring onion and a squeeze of lime.

recipes.title: Crispy tofu and herb noodle salad
recipes.blurb: Cool rice noodles with golden tofu, mint, coriander and a sweet-sharp lime and chilli dressing.

ingredients.name: Firm tofu
ingredients.prep: cut into cubes and patted dry

steps: Soak the noodles in just-boiled water for 6 to 8 minutes, then drain and rinse under cold water.
Stir the soy sauce, sugar, garlic, half the chilli and the juice of 1½ limes with 3 tbsp of water until the sugar dissolves.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over a medium-high heat and fry the tofu for 8 minutes, turning, until crisp on all sides. Toss with 1 tbsp of the dressing.
Toss the noodles with the cucumber, carrot, mint and coriander.
Divide into bowls, top with the tofu, pour over the remaining dressing and finish with the peanuts, remaining chilli and a lime wedge.

recipes.title: Chicken satay with coconut rice and cucumber
recipes.blurb: Peanut-marinated chicken pan-grilled until charred, served with a warm satay sauce and cooling cucumber.
steps: Mix the chicken with half the soy sauce, half the garlic, the ginger and 10 g of the peanut butter. Marinate for 10 minutes.
Rinse the rice and cook it in a lidded pan with the coconut milk and 150 ml of water: bring to the boil, cover, reduce to the lowest heat for 12 minutes and rest off the heat.
For the sauce, warm the remaining peanut butter, soy sauce, garlic and sweet chilli sauce in a small pan with 100 ml of water and the juice of half the lime, stirring until smooth and glossy.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan over a high heat and fry the chicken for 7 to 8 minutes, turning, until charred and cooked through.
Serve the chicken on the rice with the cucumber and coriander, the sauce spooned over and the remaining lime in wedges.

recipes.title: Vegetable nasi goreng with a fried egg
recipes.blurb: Sweet, smoky and spicy Indonesian fried rice with peas and carrots, topped with a crisp-edged egg.
steps: Cook the rice in a lidded pan with 300 ml of water: boil, cover, reduce to the lowest heat for 12 minutes, then spread on a tray to cool for a few minutes.
Mix the soy sauce, sriracha and sugar with 1 tbsp of water.
Heat 2 tbsp of the oil in a wok over a medium-high heat. Fry the shallots, garlic and chilli for 2 minutes, then add the carrot for 2 minutes more.
Add the rice and toss for 3 minutes, then add the peas and sauce and stir-fry for 2 minutes until sticky and hot.
Fry the eggs in the remaining oil in a small pan until the whites are crisp and the yolks runny.
Serve the rice topped with the eggs, with the cucumber and spring onion on the side.

recipes.title: Gado-gado with crispy tofu and peanut sauce
recipes.blurb: Warm potatoes, green beans, cabbage and bean sprouts under crispy tofu and a thick, lime-bright peanut sauce.

ingredients.name: Firm tofu
ingredients.prep: cut into cubes and patted dry

steps: Boil the potatoes in salted water for 12 to 14 minutes until tender. Add the green beans for the last 3 minutes, then drain.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over a medium-high heat and fry the tofu for 8 minutes, turning, until crisp and golden.
Whisk the peanut butter, soy sauce, sweet chilli sauce, garlic, chilli, the juice of the lime and 100 ml of warm water until smooth and pourable.
Pour boiling water over the cabbage and bean sprouts in a bowl, leave for 30 seconds, then drain well so they stay crunchy but lose their raw edge.
Arrange the potatoes, beans, cabbage, bean sprouts and cucumber on plates, top with the tofu and pour over the peanut sauce.

recipes.title: Coq au vin with buttery mash
recipes.blurb: Chicken, bacon and mushrooms braised in red wine until the sauce is glossy and savoury, with buttery mash.
steps: Put the potatoes in a pan of well-salted cold water, bring to the boil and simmer for 15–18 minutes until completely tender.
Meanwhile, heat the oil in a deep frying pan over a medium-high heat and brown the chicken for 4–5 minutes per side with a pinch of salt and pepper. Lift it out and set aside.
In the same pan fry the lardons, shallots and carrot for 5 minutes until golden, then add the mushrooms and garlic and cook for 3 minutes more.

Stir in the tomato puree and flour, then pour in the red wine and let it bubble hard for 3–4 minutes, scraping up the sticky bits from the pan. Add the stock cube dissolved in 100 ml of boiling water, the thyme and the bay leaf.
Return the chicken, cover and simmer gently for 20–25 minutes, until the chicken is tender and the sauce has thickened. Remove the bay leaf and thyme stalks.
Drain the potatoes, mash with the butter and milk and season well. Serve the chicken over the mash, scattered with the parsley.

recipes.title: Croque monsieur with a sharp green salad
recipes.blurb: Ham and mustard sandwiches under a blanket of bubbling Gruyere béchamel, with crisp leaves to cut the richness.
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Melt half the butter in a small pan, stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute, then whisk in the milk a little at a time. Simmer for 3–4 minutes until thick, then stir in half the Gruyere and season.
Toast the bread lightly, then butter one side of each slice with the remaining butter.
Spread the unbuttered sides of half the slices with the mustard and cover with the ham. Top with the remaining slices, buttered side up, and set on a baking tray.
Spoon the cheese sauce over the sandwiches and scatter with the rest of the Gruyere.
Bake for 10–12 minutes until bubbling and golden in patches.
Whisk the vinegar, oil and a pinch of salt and pepper, toss through the leaves and serve alongside.

recipes.title: Provençal vegetable tian with thyme lentils
recipes.blurb: Overlapping rings of courgette, tomato and aubergine roasted until sweet and jammy, served on garlicky lentils.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Soften the onion and sliced garlic in 10 ml of the oil for 5 minutes, then spread across the base of a shallow baking dish.
Arrange the courgette, aubergine and tomato slices upright in overlapping rows on top of the onions, alternating them as you go.

Drizzle with 20 ml of the oil, scatter over the thyme leaves, salt and pepper, and cover with foil. Bake for 25 minutes, then uncover and bake for 15–20 minutes more until soft and lightly caramelised.
While the tian bakes, simmer the lentils with the stock cube in plenty of water for 20–25 minutes until tender. Drain.
Warm the crushed garlic in the remaining oil for 30 seconds, stir through the lentils with the balsamic and parsley, and season.
Serve the tian on the lentils with the baking juices spooned over.

recipes.title: Chicken in dijon cream with leeks and buttered rice
recipes.blurb: Golden chicken breast in a silky mustard and white wine sauce with soft leeks, spooned over fluffy buttered rice.
steps: Rinse the rice, then cook in boiling salted water for 10–12 minutes until tender. Drain, return to the pan and stir through half the butter.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over a medium-high heat and cook the chicken for 5–6 minutes until golden. Lift out onto a plate.
Add the remaining butter and the leeks to the pan with a pinch of salt and cook gently for 6–7 minutes until soft. Stir in the garlic for 30 seconds.

Pour in the wine and bubble for 2 minutes until almost gone. Add the stock cube dissolved in 80 ml of boiling water, then whisk in the mustard and cream. Simmer for 3 minutes until slightly thickened.
Return the chicken and any juices to the pan and simmer for 3 minutes until cooked through. Season with pepper and serve over the rice with the parsley.

recipes.title: Cassoulet-style lentil and sausage stew with herby crumb
recipes.blurb: Pork sausages and smoky bacon simmered with lentils and tomato, finished with a crisp garlic breadcrumb topping.
steps: Heat half the oil in a large, lidded pan over a medium heat and brown the sausages all over for 6–8 minutes. Lift out and slice thickly.
Fry the bacon, onion, carrot and celery in the same pan for 6–8 minutes until soft, adding 2 of the garlic cloves for the last minute.
Stir in the tomato puree, lentils, chopped tomatoes, thyme, bay leaf and the stock cube dissolved in 500 ml of boiling water. Return the sausage slices.
Bring to a simmer, cover and cook for 25–30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the lentils are tender and the stew is thick. Add a splash of water if it gets dry.
Meanwhile, fry the panko in the remaining oil with the last garlic clove for 2–3 minutes until golden, then stir in half the parsley.
Season the stew, remove the bay leaf and serve topped with the crumb and the rest of the parsley.

recipes.title: Gratin dauphinois with pan-fried steak and green beans
recipes.blurb: Silky garlic-cream potatoes with a golden Gruyere top, beside a seared steak and snappy beans.
steps: Heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan). Warm the cream, milk, garlic, and half the salt and pepper in a large pan until just steaming, then add the potato slices and simmer gently for 5 minutes, stirring so they don't stick.
Rub a baking dish with half the butter, tip in the potatoes and cream, and press level. Scatter with the Gruyere.
Bake for 35–40 minutes until bubbling, golden on top and a knife slides into the potatoes with no resistance. Rest for 5 minutes.

Meanwhile, pat the steak dry and season. Heat the oil in a heavy frying pan until very hot and sear for 2–4 minutes per side depending on thickness, adding the remaining butter for the last minute. Rest for 5 minutes, then slice.
Boil the beans in salted water for 4 minutes until tender but still snappy, and drain. Serve everything together with the pan juices spooned over the steak.

recipes.title: Niçoise salad with tuna, eggs and olives
recipes.blurb: Tuna, soft eggs, warm potatoes, green beans and olives under a punchy mustard dressing.
steps: Boil the potatoes in salted water for 12–15 minutes until tender, adding the green beans for the last 4 minutes. Drain well.
Lower the eggs into a pan of simmering water for 7 minutes, then cool under cold running water and peel.
Whisk the mustard, vinegar, oil and a pinch of salt and pepper into a dressing.
Toss the warm potatoes and beans with half the dressing so they soak it up.
Arrange the leaves on plates and pile on the potatoes, beans, tomatoes, olives and spring onions. Top with the tuna and halved eggs, then drizzle with the remaining dressing.

recipes.title: Pissaladière-style onion and olive tart
recipes.blurb: Slow-cooked sweet onions, black olives and thyme on crisp puff pastry, served with a peppery rocket salad.
steps: Heat 20 ml of the oil in a wide pan over a medium-low heat. Add the onions, sugar and a good pinch of salt and cook for 20–25 minutes, stirring now and then, until soft, sweet and deep golden. Stir in the garlic and half the thyme for the last 2 minutes.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Unroll the pastry on a baking tray and score a border 2 cm in from the edge, without cutting through. Prick the middle with a fork.
Spread the onions inside the border, then scatter over the olives and tomatoes. Add the remaining thyme.
Bake for 20–25 minutes until the pastry is risen and golden underneath.
Dress the rocket with the remaining oil and pepper, and serve with the tart cut into squares.

recipes.title: Fish en papillote with fennel, lemon and baby potatoes
recipes.blurb: White fish steamed in a paper parcel with fennel, tomatoes, capers and a splash of white wine, so everything stays juicy.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Boil the potatoes in salted water for 12–15 minutes until tender, then drain and toss with the parsley and half the butter.
Toss the fennel with the oil and a pinch of salt, and divide between 2 large squares of baking parchment, piling it in the middle. Add the tomatoes and capers.
Season the fish and lay a fillet on each pile. Top with the lemon slices, a share of the remaining butter, a squeeze of the lemon juice and 30 ml of white wine for each parcel.
Fold the paper over and crimp the edges tightly to seal into parcels. Set on a baking tray.
Bake for 15–18 minutes until the parcels are puffed. Open carefully at the table, as the steam is hot, and serve with the potatoes.

recipes.title: French onion and Gruyere galette
recipes.blurb: Free-form puff pastry piled with jammy onions and nutty Gruyere, with a mustardy leaf salad.
steps: Melt the butter with half the oil in a wide pan over a medium-low heat, add the onions and a pinch of salt and cook for 20–25 minutes, stirring often, until soft and golden. Stir in the thyme leaves and set aside to cool a little.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Unroll the pastry onto a lined baking tray and spread the centre with half of the mustard, leaving a 3 cm border.
Scatter over half the cheese, pile on the onions and top with the rest of the cheese. Fold the border up and over the edge of the filling, pleating as you go.
Brush the pastry with the beaten egg and bake for 22–25 minutes until deep golden and the cheese is bubbling.
Whisk the remaining mustard with the vinegar, the remaining oil and pepper, toss through the leaves and serve beside the galette.

recipes.title: Bratwurst with apple sauerkraut and mustard mash
recipes.blurb: Browned German sausages on wholegrain mustard mash, with warm, sweet-sour sauerkraut and apple.
steps: Boil the potatoes in well-salted water for 15–18 minutes until tender.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan over a medium heat and brown the sausages for 10–12 minutes, turning, until cooked through. Lift out.
Add the onion to the pan and fry for 5 minutes until soft. Stir in the caraway seeds, sauerkraut and apple, with a splash of water, and cook for 5 minutes until the apple has softened.
Drain the potatoes and mash with the butter, milk and a pinch of pepper. Beat in the wholegrain mustard.
Serve the sausages on the mash with the warm sauerkraut alongside.

recipes.title: Käsespätzle-style cheesy noodles with crispy onions
recipes.blurb: Egg noodles tossed through molten Gruyere and cream, crowned with deeply browned onions and chives.
steps: Melt half the butter in a wide frying pan over a medium heat and fry the onions with a pinch of salt for 15–18 minutes, stirring often, until deeply golden and crisp at the edges.
Cook the noodles in boiling salted water according to the packet, usually 4–5 minutes, then drain, keeping a mugful of the cooking water.
Return the noodles to the warm pan with the remaining butter, the cream and two thirds of the Gruyere, and toss over a low heat, adding a splash of the cooking water until the sauce is glossy.
Tip into a small ovenproof dish, top with the rest of the cheese and cook under a hot grill for 3–4 minutes until bubbling and speckled.
Dress the leaves with the vinegar, oil and pepper. Top the noodles with the crispy onions and chives and serve with the salad.

recipes.title: Braised red cabbage with sausages and buttery potatoes
recipes.blurb: Sweet-sour cabbage braised with apple, caraway and allspice, beside plump browned sausages.
steps: Melt 15 g of the butter in a large, lidded pan over a medium heat and soften the onion for 5 minutes. Stir in the caraway and allspice for 30 seconds.

Add the cabbage, apple, vinegar, sugar, bay leaf, 100 ml of water and a good pinch of salt. Stir, cover and cook gently for 30–35 minutes, stirring now and then, until the cabbage is tender and glossy.
Meanwhile, boil the potatoes in salted water for 12–15 minutes until tender. Drain and toss with the remaining butter and the parsley.
Brown the sausages in a frying pan without extra fat for 10–12 minutes, turning, until cooked through.
Remove the bay leaf, season the cabbage with pepper and serve with the sausages and potatoes.

recipes.title: German beef goulash soup with sour cream
recipes.blurb: A paprika-red soup of tender beef, peppers and potato, brightened with a spoonful of sour cream.

ingredients.name: White potatoes
ingredients.prep: peeled and cut into 1.5 cm cubes

steps: Heat the oil in a large pan over a medium-high heat and brown the beef for 4–5 minutes, then lift out. Lower the heat and cook the onions for 6–8 minutes until soft and golden.
Stir in the tomato puree, both paprikas and the caraway seeds for 1 minute, taking care not to let the paprika catch.
Add the pepper, carrot, chopped tomatoes, the stock cube and 700 ml of water, and return the beef. Bring to the boil, then simmer gently for 20 minutes.
Add the potatoes and simmer for 12–15 minutes more, until both beef and potatoes are tender and the soup has thickened slightly.
Season well, ladle into bowls and top with the sour cream and parsley.

recipes.title: Flammkuchen-style tart with onions and mushrooms
recipes.blurb: A crisp, thin tart spread with creme fraiche, caramelised onions, mushrooms and Gruyere.
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan) with a large baking tray inside. Fry the onions and mushrooms in 15 ml of the oil with a pinch of salt for 8–10 minutes until soft and lightly browned.
Unroll the pastry on a sheet of baking parchment and roll it a little thinner. Prick all over with a fork.
Season the creme fraiche with salt and pepper and spread it over the pastry, leaving a 1 cm border. Scatter over the onions, mushrooms and Gruyere.
Slide the parchment onto the hot tray and bake for 15–18 minutes until the edges are puffed and golden and the base is crisp.
Toss the rocket with the remaining oil, scatter over the tart with the chives and serve cut into wedges.

recipes.title: Königsberger Klopse-style meatballs in caper sauce
recipes.blurb: Tender poached meatballs in a creamy lemon and caper sauce, served with buttery new potatoes.
steps: Soak the bread in the milk for 5 minutes, then squeeze out the excess and mash in a bowl with both minces, the egg, half the onion, half the capers, a good pinch of salt and pepper. Shape into 10 balls.
Boil the potatoes in salted water for 12–15 minutes until tender, then drain.

Bring 500 ml of water and the stock cube to a gentle simmer in a wide pan. Add the meatballs and poach for 12–15 minutes until cooked through. Lift out with a slotted spoon and measure out 300 ml of the stock.
In a clean pan, soften the remaining onion in half the butter for 3 minutes, stir in the flour for 1 minute, then whisk in the measured stock to make a smooth sauce. Simmer for 4 minutes.
Off the heat, stir in the creme fraiche, the remaining capers, a squeeze of lemon juice and pepper. Return the meatballs to warm through.
Toss the potatoes with the remaining butter and parsley and serve with the meatballs and sauce.

recipes.title: German potato and leek soup with rye croutons
recipes.blurb: A thick, savoury potato soup warmed with caraway and paprika, with crunchy rye croutons on top.
steps: Heat half the oil in a large pan over a medium heat and soften the onion, leek, carrot and celery for 8 minutes. Stir in the caraway and paprika for 1 minute.
Add the potatoes, bay leaf and the stock cube dissolved in 800 ml of boiling water. Bring to the boil, then simmer for 20 minutes until the potatoes are very soft.
Meanwhile, toss the rye cubes with the remaining oil and a pinch of salt and bake at 200°C (180°C fan) for 8–10 minutes until crisp.
Remove the bay leaf and crush about a third of the potatoes against the side of the pan with a spoon to thicken the soup. Stir in the mustard and season.
Ladle into bowls and top with the croutons and parsley.

recipes.title: Swedish meatballs with cream gravy, mash and lingonberries
recipes.blurb: Allspice-scented meatballs in a rich cream gravy, with buttery mash, lingonberry jam and quick-pickled cucumber.
steps: Boil the potatoes in well-salted water for 15–18 minutes until tender. Toss the cucumber with the vinegar, sugar and a pinch of salt and leave to pickle.
Mix the panko with half the milk for 5 minutes, then combine with both minces, the onion, egg, allspice, a good pinch of salt and pepper. Shape into about 16 small balls.
Melt half the butter in a large frying pan over a medium heat and fry the meatballs for 8–10 minutes, turning, until browned and cooked through. Lift out.

Stir the flour into the pan juices for 1 minute, then gradually whisk in the stock cube dissolved in 250 ml of boiling water. Add the cream and simmer for 4–5 minutes until silky, then return the meatballs.
Mash the potatoes with the remaining butter and milk and season.
Serve the meatballs and gravy over the mash with the lingonberry jam and pickled cucumber.

recipes.title: Pyttipanna with fried eggs and pickles
recipes.blurb: A crisp Swedish hash of potato, onion, carrot and beetroot, topped with runny fried eggs and a dab of mustard.

ingredients.name: White potatoes
ingredients.prep: peeled and cut into 1 cm cubes

steps: Boil the potato and carrot cubes in salted water for 5 minutes until just tender, then drain well and let the steam escape for 2 minutes.
Heat the oil and half the butter in a large non-stick frying pan over a medium-high heat and fry the potato and carrot for 8–10 minutes, turning only now and then, until golden and crisp.
Add the onion and cook for 4–5 minutes until soft, then fold in the beetroot for 2 minutes just to warm through. Season well.
Push the hash to the sides, add the remaining butter and fry the eggs in the gap for 2–3 minutes until the whites are set and the yolks still runny.
Serve the hash topped with the eggs, with the gherkins, mustard and parsley alongside.

recipes.title: Salmon with dill butter potatoes and creamy peas
recipes.blurb: Crisp-skinned salmon, new potatoes in dill butter and sweet peas stirred through lemony creme fraiche.
steps: Boil the potatoes in salted water for 12–15 minutes until tender, then drain and toss with the butter and two thirds of the dill.

Pat the salmon dry and season the skin generously. Heat the oil in a frying pan over a medium-high heat and cook skin side down for 4–5 minutes, pressing gently, until the skin is crisp. Flip and cook for 2–3 minutes more.
Meanwhile, simmer the peas and spring onions in a little water for 3 minutes, drain, then stir through the creme fraiche with the finely grated lemon zest, a squeeze of juice and some pepper.
Serve the salmon on the potatoes with the creamy peas, the remaining dill and the rest of the lemon cut into wedges.

recipes.title: Danish open sandwich supper on rye
recipes.blurb: Buttered rye topped three ways: egg and chive, beetroot and cream cheese, dill cucumber with radish.
steps: Lower the eggs into simmering water for 9 minutes, then cool under cold running water, peel and slice.
Stir the mayonnaise with half the chives and a pinch of salt and pepper. Mix the cream cheese with the mustard and a little pepper.
Butter the rye slices and spread half of them with the mustard cream cheese. Layer the beetroot on top and add a few rings of red onion.
Arrange the sliced eggs on half the remaining slices, dollop with the chive mayo and scatter over the remaining chives.
Cover the remaining slices with the cucumber and radish, sprinkle with torn dill and a pinch of salt. Serve the sandwiches with the rest of the onion rings.

recipes.title: Finnish-style creamy salmon soup
recipes.blurb: Soft potatoes, leeks and carrot in a light cream broth, with chunks of salmon, allspice and plenty of dill.
steps: Melt the butter in a large pan over a medium heat and soften the leek for 4–5 minutes without browning.
Add the potatoes, carrot, allspice, bay leaf and the stock cube dissolved in 700 ml of boiling water. Simmer for 12–15 minutes until the vegetables are tender.
Pour in the cream and bring back to a gentle simmer, then season with salt and pepper.
Slide in the salmon and poach very gently for 4–5 minutes until just opaque. Don't stir hard or it will break up.
Remove the bay leaf, stir through most of the dill, and serve with lemon wedges and the remaining dill on top.

recipes.title: Norwegian-style fish cakes with peas and chive creme fraiche
recipes.blurb: Soft, lightly spiced white fish cakes fried in butter, with sweet peas and a lemony chive sauce.
steps: Blitz the fish in a food processor with the salt for 30 seconds into a thick paste. Add the flour, egg, onion, allspice and pepper, and pulse to combine, then pulse in the milk a little at a time until the mixture is soft but holds its shape.
Stir the creme fraiche with the chives, a squeeze of lemon juice and a pinch of salt and pepper.
Melt the butter in a large non-stick frying pan over a medium heat. Spoon in the mixture to make 6 patties, flattening them gently, and fry for 4–5 minutes per side until golden and cooked through.
Meanwhile, boil the peas for 3 minutes, drain and season.
Serve the fish cakes with the peas, the chive creme fraiche and the remaining lemon cut into wedges.

recipes.title: Nordic roast beetroot, lentil and apple bowl
recipes.blurb: Sweet roasted beetroot and crisp apple on mustardy lentils with walnuts and dill.

ingredients.name: Cooked beetroot
ingredients.prep: raw, peeled and cut into wedges

steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Toss the beetroot and red onion with half the oil and a good pinch of salt on a large tray and roast for 30–35 minutes until tender and caramelised at the edges.
Meanwhile, simmer the lentils in plenty of unsalted water for 20–25 minutes until tender but still holding their shape. Drain.
Whisk the mustard, vinegar, maple syrup, the remaining oil, salt and pepper into a dressing and stir half of it through the warm lentils.
Toast the walnuts in a dry pan for 2–3 minutes until fragrant.
Divide the leaves and lentils between bowls, top with the roasted beetroot and onion, apple, walnuts and dill, and drizzle with the rest of the dressing.

recipes.title: Mushroom toad in the hole-style with sage onion gravy
recipes.blurb: Big roasted mushrooms in a tall, crisp Yorkshire batter with sticky sage onion gravy and peas.
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Whisk 120 g of the flour with the eggs, milk, half the sage, a pinch of salt and pepper until smooth, then leave to stand while the oven heats.
Pour the oil into a metal roasting tin or ovenproof dish, add the mushrooms, and roast for 10 minutes until the tin is smoking hot.

Pour the batter quickly into the sizzling tin around the mushrooms and return it to the oven straight away. Bake for 25–30 minutes without opening the door, until the batter is puffed, deep golden and crisp.

Meanwhile, melt the butter in a pan and cook the onions with a pinch of salt for 12–15 minutes until soft and golden, adding the rest of the sage for the last 2 minutes. Stir in the remaining flour for 1 minute, then add the balsamic and the stock cube dissolved in 300 ml of boiling water. Simmer for 5 minutes until glossy.
Boil the peas for 3 minutes and drain. Serve the toad in the hole cut into wedges with the gravy and peas.

recipes.title: Creamy fish pie with spinach and cheddar mash
recipes.blurb: White fish and salmon in a parsley cream sauce with peas and spinach, under a golden cheddar mash.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Boil the potatoes in salted water for 15–18 minutes until tender, then drain and mash with half the butter, a splash of the milk and most of the cheddar. Season.

Melt the remaining butter in a pan, stir in the flour for 1 minute, then whisk in the rest of the milk a little at a time. Simmer for 4–5 minutes until thick, stirring, then add the mustard, parsley and a pinch of salt and pepper.
Wilt the spinach in a colander with boiling water, squeeze out the excess liquid and chop roughly.
Gently fold the fish, peas and spinach into the sauce and spoon into a baking dish.
Top with the mash, rough it up with a fork and scatter with the last of the cheddar.
Bake for 25–30 minutes until the sauce is bubbling at the edges and the top is golden.

recipes.title: Smoky bean and sweet potato cottage pie
recipes.blurb: A rich mushroom and bean filling under crisp-edged sweet potato mash, with a smoky paprika kick.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Boil the sweet potato in salted water for 12–15 minutes until soft, then drain well and mash with half the oil, salt and pepper.
Meanwhile, heat the remaining oil in a large pan and cook the onion, carrot and mushrooms for 8–10 minutes until soft and golden. Add the garlic and smoked paprika for 1 minute.
Stir in the tomato puree, chopped tomatoes, both beans and the stock cube dissolved in 150 ml of boiling water. Simmer for 10 minutes until thick, adding the peas for the last 2 minutes. Season.
Spoon the filling into a baking dish, cover with the sweet potato mash and rough the top up with a fork.
Bake for 20–25 minutes until the top is crisp-edged and the filling is bubbling.

recipes.title: Bubble and squeak cakes with fried eggs
recipes.blurb: Crisp-edged potato and cabbage cakes topped with runny fried eggs, with a good squirt of ketchup.
steps: Boil the potatoes in salted water for 12–15 minutes until tender. Drain, leave to steam dry for 2 minutes, then mash roughly with the butter, salt and pepper.
Heat half the oil in a frying pan over a medium heat and fry the onion and cabbage for 6–8 minutes until soft and starting to brown. Tip into the mash and mix well.
Shape the mixture into 4 thick patties.
Wipe out the pan, heat the remaining oil over a medium-high heat and fry the cakes for 4–5 minutes per side until deeply golden and crisp. Keep them warm.
Fry the eggs in the same pan for 2–3 minutes until the whites are set and the yolks runny. Serve two cakes per person, each topped with an egg, and the ketchup alongside.

recipes.title: Punjabi chana masala with ginger and basmati
recipes.blurb: Chickpeas simmered in a tangy tomato and ginger gravy, finished with lemon and fresh coriander.
steps: Rinse the rice, then cook it in plenty of boiling salted water for 10–12 minutes until tender. Drain and keep covered.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over a medium heat and fry the onion for 8 minutes until soft and golden. Add the garlic, ginger and green chilli and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the cumin, ground coriander, turmeric and chilli powder and cook for 30 seconds, then tip in the tomatoes and a pinch of salt.
Add the chickpeas with 150 ml of water. Simmer for 12–15 minutes, pressing a few chickpeas against the side of the pan to thicken the sauce.
Stir in the garam masala and a squeeze of lemon, taste for salt, and scatter with coriander. Serve over the rice with the remaining lemon cut into wedges.

recipes.title: Rajma, Punjabi kidney bean curry with rice
recipes.blurb: Soft kidney beans in a deep, mellow tomato gravy, the Sunday comfort dish of Punjabi homes.
steps: Heat the oil in a saucepan over a medium heat and cook the onion for 10 minutes, stirring often, until deep golden. Stir in the garlic and ginger for 1 minute.
Add the cumin, ground coriander, turmeric and chilli powder, then the tomato puree, and cook for 2 minutes until the oil starts to separate.
Pour in the chopped tomatoes and a pinch of salt and simmer for 8 minutes until the sauce has thickened and darkened.
Add the kidney beans and 200 ml of water. Simmer for 12 minutes, mashing about a quarter of the beans with the back of a spoon so the gravy turns creamy.
Meanwhile, cook the rice in boiling salted water for 10–12 minutes, then drain.
Stir the garam masala into the rajma, check the salt and serve over the rice with coriander on top.

recipes.title: Butter chicken-style curry with basmati
recipes.blurb: yoghurt-marinated chicken in a silky, mildly spiced tomato and butter sauce.
steps: Mix the chicken with the yoghurt, half the garam masala, the cumin, half the paprika, half the garlic, half the ginger and a pinch of salt. Leave to marinate while you start the sauce, or for up to a few hours if you have time.
Heat the oil and half the butter in a wide pan over a medium heat. Fry the onion for 8 minutes until soft, then add the remaining garlic and ginger for 1 minute.
Add the remaining garam masala and paprika, then the passata, sugar and a pinch of salt. Simmer for 10 minutes until thickened.
Meanwhile, cook the rice in boiling salted water for 10–12 minutes, then drain.
Add the chicken and its marinade to the sauce and simmer gently for 12–15 minutes, stirring now and then, until the chicken is cooked through.
Stir in the cream and the remaining butter, warm through for 2 minutes and serve over the rice with coriander.

recipes.title: Sambar-style lentil and vegetable stew with rice
recipes.blurb: A tangy South Indian lentil stew of aubergine, carrot and tomato, lifted with tamarind, mustard seeds and curry leaves.
steps: Put the lentils, carrot, turmeric and 700 ml of water in a large pan. Bring to the boil, then simmer for 10 minutes, skimming off any foam.
Add the aubergine, tomatoes, ground coriander, cumin, chilli powder, green chilli and salt. Simmer for 15 minutes until the vegetables are soft and the lentils have broken down into a loose stew.
Meanwhile, cook the rice in boiling salted water for 10–12 minutes, then drain.
Stir the tamarind into the stew and taste; it should be gently sour and savoury, so add a little more salt if it needs it.

In a small pan, heat the oil until hot and add the mustard seeds. When they pop, add the curry leaves (stand back, they spit) and fry for 10 seconds, then add the onion and garlic and fry for 4–5 minutes until golden.
Tip the sizzling tarka over the stew, stir through half the coriander and serve with the rice and the rest of the coriander.

recipes.title: Kerala-style coconut fish curry with rice
recipes.blurb: White fish poached in a sour, gently hot coconut sauce with mustard seeds, curry leaves and tamarind.
steps: Cook the rice in boiling salted water for 10–12 minutes, then drain and keep covered.

Heat the oil in a wide pan over a medium heat and add the mustard seeds. When they start to pop, add the curry leaves (stand back, they spit) for 10 seconds, then the onion, and fry for 6 minutes until soft.
Stir in the garlic, ginger and green chilli for 1 minute, then the turmeric, ground coriander and chilli powder for 30 seconds.
Add the tomato, coconut milk, tamarind and a good pinch of salt. Simmer gently for 6–8 minutes until the tomato has softened into the sauce.
Slide in the fish, spoon the sauce over and cook gently for 5–6 minutes until it flakes. Try not to stir too much, or the fish will break up.
Taste for salt and sourness, scatter over the coriander and serve with the rice.

recipes.title: South Indian lemon rice with cashews and peas
recipes.blurb: Fragrant, sunny rice with crackling mustard seeds, curry leaves, toasted cashews and a sharp lemon hit.
steps: Rinse the rice, then cook it in plenty of boiling salted water for 10–12 minutes. Add the peas for the last 2 minutes, then drain well and spread out on a plate so it stays fluffy.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan over a medium heat. Add the cashews and fry for 1–2 minutes until golden, then lift them out with a slotted spoon.
In the same oil, add the mustard seeds and cover loosely until they stop popping, about 30 seconds. Add the curry leaves for 10 seconds until crisp.
Stir in the green chilli, ginger and turmeric for 30 seconds, then tip in the rice and peas and toss until every grain is yellow.
Take off the heat. Add the zest of 1 lemon and the juice of both, the cashews and half the coriander, and season to taste.
Serve scattered with the rest of the coriander.

recipes.title: Goan prawn xacuti-style curry with rice
recipes.blurb: Plump prawns in a warm, nutty coconut sauce scented with cinnamon, star anise and tamarind.
steps: Toast the sesame seeds in a dry pan for 1–2 minutes until golden, then tip into a mug and set aside.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over a medium heat and fry the onion for 8 minutes until golden. Add the garlic, ginger and red chilli for 1 minute.
Stir in the ground coriander, cumin, cinnamon, star anise, chilli powder and black pepper and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Pour in the coconut milk, add the tamarind, sesame seeds and salt, and simmer for 10 minutes until the sauce is rich and slightly reduced. Fish out the star anise.
Meanwhile, cook the rice in boiling salted water for 10–12 minutes, then drain.
Add the prawns to the sauce and cook for 3–4 minutes until pink and curled. Finish with a squeeze of lime, scatter over the coriander and serve with the rice and lime wedges.

recipes.title: Pork vindaloo-style curry with potatoes
recipes.blurb: Tender pork and potato in a sharp, fiery vinegar and chilli sauce, closer to Goa than the takeaway.

ingredients.name: White potatoes
ingredients.prep: peeled and cut into 3 cm chunks

steps: Stir the pork with the vinegar, half the garlic, half the ginger, the chilli powder, paprika, cumin, turmeric, ground coriander, cinnamon and half the salt. Leave for at least 10 minutes while you prepare the rest.

Heat the oil in a heavy pan over a medium heat, add the mustard seeds and let them pop for 20 seconds. Add the onion and fry for 8 minutes until golden, then stir in the remaining garlic and ginger for 1 minute.
Add the tomato puree and the sugar and cook for 1 minute, then tip in the marinated pork and brown for 4 minutes, stirring.
Pour in 300 ml of water, add the potatoes and the remaining salt, cover and simmer gently for 30 minutes until the pork is tender and the potatoes are cooked.
Uncover for the last 5 minutes if the sauce is thin, and let it reduce until it clings. Taste for salt, sour and heat.
Cook the rice in boiling salted water for 10–12 minutes while the curry finishes, drain, and serve alongside.

recipes.title: Bengali-style mustard fish with rice
recipes.blurb: White fish in a pungent mustard and yoghurt sauce, sharp, hot and quick to make.
steps: Soak the mustard seeds in 80 ml of warm water for 10 minutes. Meanwhile, rub the fish with half the turmeric, a pinch of salt and a squeeze of lemon.
Blitz the soaked seeds and their water with the green chilli, yoghurt, a pinch of salt and the juice of ½ lemon in a small blender until you have a coarse, pungent paste.
Cook the rice in boiling salted water for 10–12 minutes, then drain.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over a medium heat, fry the onion for 5 minutes until soft, then add the remaining turmeric for 30 seconds.

Pour in the mustard paste with 100 ml of water and bring to a gentle simmer. Lay in the fish and cook for 6–8 minutes, spooning the sauce over, until the fish flakes. Don't boil it hard or the sauce can turn bitter.
Scatter with the coriander and serve with the rice and the remaining lemon in wedges.

recipes.title: Gujarati dal dhokli-style one-pot
recipes.blurb: Spiced flatbread diamonds simmered in a sweet-sour lentil broth with peanuts, a real one-pot supper.
steps: Make the dough: mix the flour with half the turmeric, half the cumin, 1 teaspoon of salt, 10 ml of the oil and about 60 ml of water until it comes together. Knead for 2 minutes, cover and rest.
Put the lentils in a large pan with 800 ml of water and the remaining turmeric. Bring to the boil, then simmer for 15 minutes until soft and starting to collapse.

Meanwhile, heat the remaining oil in a small pan, add the mustard seeds and, when they pop, the garlic, ginger and green chilli for 1 minute. Add the remaining cumin, ground coriander and chilli powder, then the tomatoes, and cook for 4 minutes.
Stir the tomato mixture into the lentils with the tamarind, sugar, peanuts and the remaining salt. Simmer for 5 minutes.
Roll the dough out as thin as you can, about 2 mm, and cut it into small diamonds with a knife.

Drop the diamonds into the simmering dal, stirring gently, and cook for 8–10 minutes until they are tender. Add a splash of water if it gets too thick, then stir through the coriander and serve in bowls.

recipes.title: Quick Hyderabadi-style chicken biryani
recipes.blurb: Marinated chicken under saffron-coloured rice, steamed in one pot with fried onions and mint.
steps: Mix the chicken with the yoghurt, garlic, ginger, garam masala, cumin, turmeric, chilli powder, half the lemon juice and 1 teaspoon of salt. Leave to marinate while you fry the onions.
Heat the oil in a wide, heavy pan with a lid over a medium-high heat. Fry the onions for 12–15 minutes, stirring often, until deep golden brown. Lift out half onto a plate for the top.
Add the chicken and its marinade to the pan with the green chilli and cook for 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until the sauce thickens and the chicken is nearly cooked.
Meanwhile, boil the rice with the bay leaves and the remaining salt in a large pan of water for 6 minutes only, so it is still firm in the middle. Drain.
Spoon the rice over the chicken in an even layer, then scatter with the reserved onions, mint and coriander. Cover the pan with foil, then the lid, to seal in the steam.
Cook on the lowest heat for 15 minutes, then rest for 5 minutes with the lid on. Squeeze over the remaining lemon and fluff the rice into the chicken to serve.

recipes.title: Aloo matar, potato and pea curry
recipes.blurb: Soft potatoes and sweet peas in a cumin-scented tomato masala, simple North Indian home cooking.

ingredients.name: White potatoes
ingredients.prep: peeled and cut into 2 cm chunks

steps: Heat the oil in a wide pan over a medium heat, add the cumin seeds and let them sizzle for 20 seconds. Add the onion and fry for 7 minutes until golden.
Stir in the garlic, ginger and green chilli for 1 minute, then the turmeric, ground coriander and chilli powder for 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 4 minutes until they break down into a thick paste.
Add the potatoes, salt and 250 ml of water. Cover and simmer for 15 minutes until the potatoes are nearly tender.
Meanwhile, cook the rice in boiling salted water for 10–12 minutes, then drain.
Stir the peas into the curry and cook for 4 minutes, uncovered, until the sauce clings. Finish with the garam masala and coriander and serve with the rice.

recipes.title: Home-style egg curry with rice
recipes.blurb: Soft-boiled-then-fried eggs in a rich onion and tomato masala, the everyday comfort curry.
steps: Lower the eggs into boiling water and cook for 8 minutes, then cool under cold running water and peel.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over a medium heat and fry the onions for 10 minutes until deep golden. Add the garlic, ginger and green chilli for 1 minute.
Stir in the cumin, ground coriander, turmeric and chilli powder for 30 seconds, then add the tomatoes and salt. Simmer for 10 minutes until thick and glossy, adding a splash of water if it catches.
Meanwhile, cook the rice in boiling salted water for 10–12 minutes, then drain.
Score each egg lightly with a knife, add to the sauce with 100 ml of water and simmer for 5 minutes, spooning the masala over.
Stir in the garam masala, scatter over the coriander and serve with the rice.

recipes.title: Palak paneer with warm naan
recipes.blurb: Golden paneer cubes in a vivid, silky spinach sauce with a little cream and gentle spice.
steps: Put the spinach in a colander and pour over a kettle of boiling water until wilted. Cool for a minute, squeeze out the excess water and blitz to a coarse purée with the garlic, ginger and green chilli.
Heat half the oil in a non-stick pan over a medium-high heat and fry the paneer for 4–5 minutes, turning, until golden on most sides. Lift out onto a plate.
Add the remaining oil and the cumin seeds to the pan, then the onion and fry for 6 minutes until soft. Add the tomato, ground coriander and salt and cook for 3 minutes.
Pour in the spinach purée with 100 ml of water and simmer for 5 minutes. Stir in the garam masala and the cream.
Return the paneer to the pan and warm through for 2 minutes, while you heat the naan according to the packet.
Serve the palak paneer straight away with the warm naan.

recipes.title: Vegetable korma with cashews and cauliflower
recipes.blurb: Cauliflower, carrot and peas in a creamy, mild coconut and cashew sauce. Dairy-free and family-friendly.
steps: Soak the cashews in 100 ml of just-boiled water for 10 minutes. Cook the rice in boiling salted water for 10–12 minutes, then drain.
Meanwhile, toast the flaked almonds in a dry pan for 2 minutes until golden, then tip out and set aside.
Blitz the onion, garlic, ginger and the cashews with their soaking water until smooth.

Heat the oil in a wide pan over a medium heat, add the blitzed paste and fry for 5 minutes, stirring, until it smells sweet and loses its raw edge. Add the ground coriander, cumin, turmeric and garam masala for 30 seconds.
Pour in the coconut milk and 100 ml of water, add the cauliflower, carrot and salt and simmer for 12 minutes until the vegetables are tender. Add the peas for the final 3 minutes.
Spoon the korma over the rice and finish with the toasted almonds and coriander.

recipes.title: Baingan bharta-style smoky aubergine with rice
recipes.blurb: Whole-roasted aubergine mashed into a smoky, spiced tomato and onion masala.
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Prick the aubergine all over with a fork, rub with 5 ml of the oil and roast on a tray for 35–40 minutes, turning once, until the skins are blistered and the flesh has collapsed.
Meanwhile, cook the rice in boiling salted water for 10–12 minutes, then drain.
Once the aubergine is cool enough to handle, split them open, scoop out the soft flesh and chop roughly, discarding the skins.
Heat the remaining oil in a wide pan over a medium heat, add the cumin seeds for 20 seconds, then the onion and fry for 7 minutes until golden. Add the garlic, ginger and green chilli for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, turmeric, ground coriander and salt and cook for 5 minutes until jammy. Stir in the aubergine flesh and the peas and cook for 5 minutes.
Finish with the garam masala and coriander, and serve with the rice.

recipes.title: Chicken jalfrezi with peppers and basmati
recipes.blurb: Quick-fried chicken with charred peppers and onion in a thick, sharp, fiery tomato masala.
steps: Cook the rice in boiling salted water for 10–12 minutes, then drain and keep covered.
Heat half the oil in a large frying pan or wok over a high heat. Fry the chicken for 5 minutes until browned, then lift out onto a plate.
Add the remaining oil and the cumin seeds, then the onion and peppers, and stir-fry for 5 minutes until charred at the edges but still crisp.
Add the garlic, ginger and green chilli for 1 minute, then the ground coriander, ground cumin, turmeric and chilli powder for 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes, salt and 50 ml of water and cook for 5 minutes until they collapse into a thick sauce. Return the chicken and any juices and cook for 4–5 minutes until cooked through.
Stir in the garam masala and coriander, and serve with the rice.

recipes.title: Paneer bhurji, spiced scramble with warm naan
recipes.blurb: Crumbled paneer scrambled with onion, tomato and green chilli, ready in twenty minutes.
steps: Crumble the paneer into small, uneven pieces with your hands and set aside.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan over a medium heat, add the cumin seeds for 20 seconds, then the onion and fry for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the green chilli, ginger and garlic for 1 minute, then the turmeric and chilli powder for 20 seconds.
Add the tomatoes and salt and cook for 4 minutes until pulpy. Stir in the peas and crumbled paneer and cook for 4 minutes, stirring, until hot through and the moisture has cooked off.
Meanwhile, warm the naan according to the packet.
Stir in the garam masala and half the coriander, squeeze over some lemon juice, and serve with the naan and the rest of the coriander.

recipes.title: Chicken tikka masala with basmati
recipes.blurb: Charred tikka chicken in a smooth, creamy tomato masala. The fakeaway favourite, done properly.
steps: Mix the chicken with half the tikka paste, the yoghurt and a pinch of salt. Leave to marinate while you start the sauce, or for longer if you can.

Heat the oil and butter in a pan over a medium heat and fry the onion for 8 minutes until soft. Add the garlic and ginger for 1 minute, then the remaining tikka paste and the tomato puree for 2 minutes.
Pour in the passata and 100 ml of water, add the sugar and simmer for 12 minutes until thick and glossy.
Meanwhile, heat the grill to high. Thread or spread the chicken on a lined tray and grill for 12–15 minutes, turning once, until charred at the edges and cooked through.
Cook the rice in boiling salted water for 10–12 minutes, then drain.
Blitz the sauce with a stick blender if you like it smooth, then stir in the cream and garam masala. Add the grilled chicken, simmer for 2 minutes and serve over the rice with coriander.

recipes.title: Mushroom and pea masala with basmati
recipes.blurb: Browned mushrooms and sweet peas in a spiced onion and tomato gravy, hearty and fully vegan.
steps: Cook the rice in boiling salted water for 10–12 minutes, then drain and keep covered.
Heat half the oil in a wide pan over a high heat and fry the mushrooms for 6–7 minutes without crowding, until browned and their water has cooked off. Tip onto a plate.
Lower the heat to medium, add the remaining oil and the cumin seeds, then the onion and cook for 6 minutes until golden. Add the garlic and ginger for 1 minute.
Stir in the ground coriander, turmeric and chilli powder for 30 seconds, then add the tomatoes and salt and simmer for 8 minutes until thick.
Return the mushrooms with the peas and 50 ml of water and cook for 4 minutes until the peas are tender.
Stir through the garam masala and coriander, and serve with the rice.

recipes.title: Chicken tikka traybake with mint raita
recipes.blurb: Marinated chicken, peppers and red onion roasted until charred, with basmati and a cool cucumber raita.
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Stir the tikka paste into 75 g of the yoghurt with the juice of half the lemon and a pinch of salt, then coat the chicken in it and leave while the oven heats.
Tip the chicken, pepper and red onion onto a large tray, drizzle with the oil and spread out so nothing is crowded.
Roast for 25 minutes, turning once, until the chicken is cooked through and the edges are blackened in places.
Meanwhile, rinse the rice, cook it in plenty of boiling salted water for 10 minutes, then drain and leave to steam dry with the lid on.
Squeeze the grated cucumber to drain it, then stir into the remaining yoghurt with the mint, a squeeze of lemon and some black pepper.
Serve the traybake over the rice with the raita and the remaining lemon cut into wedges.

recipes.title: Fiery lamb keema with peas and green chilli
recipes.blurb: Dry-fried spiced lamb mince with sweet peas and a proper chilli kick, spooned over basmati.
steps: Put the rice on to cook in boiling salted water for 10 minutes, then drain and keep covered.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over a medium heat and fry the cumin seeds for 30 seconds, then add the onion and cook for 8 minutes until golden at the edges.
Stir in the garlic, ginger and green chilli and cook for 1 minute, then add the ground coriander, chilli powder and tomato puree.
Turn the heat up, crumble in the lamb and fry for 8 minutes, breaking it up, until browned and the fat has rendered. Add a splash of water and the salt and simmer for 5 minutes.
Stir in the peas and garam masala and cook for 3 minutes until the peas are hot through.
Scatter with coriander and serve over the rice.

recipes.title: Paneer tikka and pepper traybake with lemon rice
recipes.blurb: Charred, spiced paneer and peppers on a single tray, served over lemony basmati with yoghurt.
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Mix the tikka paste with half the yoghurt and a squeeze of lemon, then fold through the paneer, peppers and onion until coated.
Spread over a large tray, drizzle with the oil and roast for 22 minutes, turning once, until the paneer is golden and the peppers are charred at the edges.
Meanwhile, rinse the rice and cook it in boiling salted water with the turmeric for 10 minutes. Drain, then stir through the zest of the lemon and a pinch of salt.
Loosen the remaining yoghurt with a little lemon juice.
Serve the traybake on the lemon rice with the yoghurt spooned over and the coriander scattered on top.

recipes.title: Red lentil tarka dal with rice
recipes.blurb: Soft turmeric lentils finished with a sizzling garlic, cumin and chilli tarka.
steps: Rinse the lentils until the water runs mostly clear. Heat half the oil in a saucepan, soften the onion for 6 minutes, then add the grated garlic, ginger and turmeric.
Add the tomatoes, lentils and 600 ml of water with the salt. Bring to the boil, then simmer for 20 minutes, stirring now and then, until the lentils have collapsed into a thick soup.
While the dal cooks, boil the rice in salted water for 10 minutes, then drain.

For the tarka, heat the remaining oil in a small pan until hot, add the cumin seeds and sliced garlic and fry for about a minute until the garlic is just golden. Take off the heat and stir in the chilli flakes.
Squeeze a little lemon into the dal and taste for salt. Pour the sizzling tarka over the top, scatter with coriander and serve with the rice.

recipes.title: Aloo gobi with fresh ginger and coriander
recipes.blurb: Dry-style potato and cauliflower curry with turmeric, cumin and a good hit of green chilli.
steps: Heat the oil in a large lidded frying pan, add the cumin seeds for 30 seconds, then the onion, and cook for 7 minutes until soft and lightly golden.
Stir in the garlic, ginger, chilli, turmeric and ground coriander and cook for 1 minute.

Add the potato, cauliflower and salt and stir to coat. Pour in the tomatoes and 100 ml of water, cover and cook over a medium-low heat for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until a knife slides easily into the potato.
Uncover and cook for 3 minutes to thicken any liquid, then stir through the garam masala and a squeeze of lemon.
Warm the naan in a dry pan or under the grill and serve alongside, topped with the coriander.

recipes.title: King prawn coconut curry with lime
recipes.blurb: Juicy prawns in a silky, gently spiced coconut sauce with ginger, tomato and a squeeze of lime.
steps: Boil the rice in salted water for 10 minutes, drain and keep covered.
Heat the oil in a deep pan and cook the onion over a medium heat for 7 minutes until soft. Add the garlic, ginger and chilli and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the turmeric, cumin, coriander, chilli powder and tomato puree and cook for 1 minute until fragrant, adding a splash of water if it catches.
Pour in the coconut milk, add the salt and simmer gently for 10 minutes until slightly thickened.
Add the prawns and cook for 3 to 4 minutes, just until pink and curled. Squeeze in the lime juice.
Serve over the rice with the coriander on top.

recipes.title: Sweet potato and chickpea coconut curry
recipes.blurb: Soft roasted sweet potato and chickpeas in a mellow, creamy curry sauce with a little warmth.
steps: Heat the oil in a large pan and cook the onion for 6 minutes. Add the garlic and ginger for 1 minute, then the curry powder and turmeric for 30 seconds.
Add the sweet potato, chopped tomatoes, coconut milk, salt and 100 ml of water. Bring to a simmer, cover and cook for 15 minutes.
Stir in the chickpeas and simmer uncovered for 8 to 10 minutes until the sweet potato is tender and the sauce coats a spoon.
Meanwhile, cook the rice in boiling salted water for 10 minutes and drain.
Fold the spinach through the curry until wilted, then finish with lime juice to taste. Serve with the rice.

recipes.title: Hot beef madras with basmati
recipes.blurb: Tender strips of beef in a deep red, chilli-heavy tomato sauce. Properly hot, balanced with a spoon of yoghurt.
steps: Heat half the oil in a heavy pan over a high heat and brown the beef in two batches for 2 minutes each. Set aside.
Lower the heat, add the remaining oil and the onion and cook for 8 minutes until soft and golden. Stir in the garlic, ginger and green chilli for 1 minute.
Add the chilli powder, chilli flakes, cumin, coriander, turmeric and tomato puree and stir for 1 minute, adding a splash of water if it sticks.
Return the beef with any juices, add the chopped tomatoes, salt, sugar and 100 ml of water. Cover and simmer gently for 20 minutes until the beef is tender and the sauce has thickened.
Meanwhile, cook the rice in boiling salted water for 10 minutes and drain.
Serve the madras over the rice with a spoonful of yoghurt and the coriander. Taste before adding more chilli, this one is hot.

recipes.title: Tandoori-style salmon with cucumber raita
recipes.blurb: Yoghurt-and-spice marinated salmon roasted hot, served with fluffy rice and a cooling raita.
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Mix 80 g of the yoghurt with the paprika, cumin, garam masala, turmeric, garlic, juice of half the lemon and a pinch of salt. Coat the salmon and leave for 10 minutes.
Boil the rice in salted water for 10 minutes and drain. Cook the green beans in the same pan for the last 4 minutes.
Place the salmon on an oiled tray and roast for 10 to 12 minutes until it flakes easily and the top is spotted with colour.
Stir the cucumber, sliced onion and mint into the remaining yoghurt with a squeeze of lemon and a pinch of salt.
Serve the salmon on the rice and beans with the raita and the remaining lemon in wedges.

recipes.title: Vegetable biryani-style rice with cashews
recipes.blurb: Fragrant spiced rice with carrot, peas, golden onion, cashews and a few sweet raisins, all in one pan.
steps: Rinse the rice in cold water until it runs clear, then leave it to drain. Heat half the oil in a wide lidded pan and fry the cashews until golden, about 2 minutes. Lift out and set aside.
Add the remaining oil and the onions and cook over a medium heat for 12 minutes, stirring often, until deep golden. Remove a third for topping.
Add the cumin seeds, bay leaves, garlic, ginger, garam masala, turmeric and cinnamon and stir for 1 minute, then add the carrot and rice and stir to coat.
Dissolve the stock cube in 330 ml of boiling water, pour it in with the salt and raisins, bring to the boil, then cover tightly and cook on the lowest heat for 12 minutes.
Scatter the peas over the top, replace the lid and leave off the heat for 8 minutes so they steam through.
Fluff with a fork, discard the bay leaves, and top with the reserved onions, cashews, coriander and a squeeze of lemon.

recipes.title: Mild chicken korma with toasted almonds
recipes.blurb: Gentle, creamy and fragrant, with no heat at all. A korma for anyone who finds a medium curry too much.
steps: Toast the almonds in a dry pan for 2 minutes until pale gold, then tip them out.
Heat the oil in a deep pan and cook the onion for 8 minutes over a gentle heat until completely soft but not coloured. Add the garlic, ginger and spices and cook for 1 minute.
Add the chicken and stir for 3 minutes to seal, then pour in the coconut milk and 100 ml of water. Season with the salt and sugar and simmer gently for 12 minutes.
Meanwhile, boil the rice in salted water for 10 minutes and drain.
Take the pan off the heat for a minute, then stir in the yoghurt and peas and return to a low heat for 2 minutes without boiling.
Serve over the rice, topped with the almonds and coriander.

recipes.title: Lamb kofta flatbreads with mint yoghurt
recipes.blurb: Spiced lamb koftas grilled until sizzling, tucked into warm pitta with crunchy salad and mint yoghurt.
steps: Heat the grill to high. In a bowl, mix the lamb with the grated onion, garlic, cumin, coriander, cinnamon, parsley, salt and pepper, and knead for a minute until sticky.
Shape into 8 oval koftas and thread onto skewers or lay on an oiled tray. Grill for 10 to 12 minutes, turning, until browned and cooked through.
Stir the mint into the yoghurt with a squeeze of lemon and a pinch of salt.
Toss the cucumber, tomato and sliced onion with the olive oil and a squeeze of lemon.
Warm the pittas for the last minute under the grill, then split them and fill with the koftas, salad and a spoonful of mint yoghurt.

recipes.title: Chicken shawarma pittas with garlic yoghurt
recipes.blurb: Spice-rubbed chicken thighs roasted until crisp at the edges, stuffed in pitta with pickled red onion and garlicky yoghurt.
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Toss the chicken with the cumin, paprika, turmeric, cinnamon, half the garlic, the oil, juice of half the lemon, salt and pepper, and leave for 10 minutes.
Put the sliced onion in a bowl with the vinegar and a pinch of salt and scrunch together. Leave to soften while the chicken cooks.
Spread the chicken on a tray and roast for 18 to 20 minutes, turning once, until cooked through and browned at the edges.
Stir the remaining garlic into the yoghurt with a squeeze of lemon and a pinch of salt.
Warm the pittas in the oven for the last 2 minutes, then fill with the chicken, cucumber, tomato, pickled onion, parsley and plenty of garlic yoghurt.

recipes.title: Smoky shakshuka with feta and warm pitta
recipes.blurb: Eggs baked in a cumin-spiced pepper and tomato sauce, finished with crumbled feta and parsley.
steps: Heat the oil in a deep, lidded frying pan and cook the onion and peppers over a medium heat for 10 minutes until soft and starting to colour.
Add the garlic, cumin, smoked paprika and chilli flakes and stir for 1 minute, then pour in the tomatoes with the salt and pepper.
Simmer for 8 minutes until the sauce is thick and jammy. Taste and adjust the seasoning.
Make a well in the sauce for each egg and crack them in. Cover and cook gently for 5 to 6 minutes until the whites are set but the yolks are still soft.
Warm the pittas in a toaster or dry pan. Crumble the feta over the shakshuka, scatter with parsley and serve straight from the pan with the pitta.

recipes.title: Halloumi fattoush with sumac and lemon
recipes.blurb: Crisp pitta, cucumber, tomato and mint with golden halloumi and a sharp sumac dressing.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Tear the pittas into rough pieces, toss with 10 ml of the oil and half the sumac, and bake on a tray for 6 to 8 minutes until crisp.
Whisk the remaining oil with the juice of the lemon, the rest of the sumac, salt and pepper in a large bowl.
Add the cucumber, tomato, little gem, radish, red onion, mint and parsley and toss to coat.
Fry the halloumi in a dry non-stick pan over a medium-high heat for 2 minutes per side until deeply golden.
Fold the crisp pitta through the salad at the last moment, so it stays crunchy, and top with the hot halloumi.

recipes.title: Crisp chickpea fritters with lemon tahini
recipes.blurb: Herby, cumin-spiced chickpea patties shallow-fried until crisp, with a lemony tahini drizzle and pickled onion.
steps: Scrunch the red onion with the vinegar and a pinch of salt and leave to pickle.

Mash the chickpeas in a bowl, leaving some texture. Mix in the flour, garlic, spring onions, cumin, ground coriander, chilli flakes, parsley, coriander and salt, and shape into 8 small patties. Chill for 10 minutes if you have time.
Whisk the tahini with the juice of half the lemon, 45 ml of cold water and a pinch of salt until smooth and pourable.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan over a medium heat and fry the patties for 3 to 4 minutes per side until deep golden and crisp. Drain on kitchen paper.
Warm the pittas and serve with the fritters, cucumber, pickled onion, tahini sauce and the remaining lemon in wedges.

recipes.title: Roast aubergine with tahini, bulgur and pomegranate
recipes.blurb: Tender, caramelised aubergine over herby bulgur with a nutty tahini sauce and jewel-like pomegranate.
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Place the aubergines cut-side up on a tray, brush generously with 30 ml of the oil, sprinkle with the cumin, salt and pepper, and roast for 30 to 35 minutes until deeply golden and completely soft.
Meanwhile, dissolve the stock cube in 250 ml of boiling water, pour it over the bulgur in a bowl, cover and leave for 15 minutes until the liquid is absorbed.
Whisk the tahini with the garlic, juice of half the lemon, 40 ml of cold water and a pinch of salt until smooth.
Fluff the bulgur with a fork and stir through the red onion, tomatoes, parsley, mint, the remaining oil and a squeeze of lemon.
Serve the aubergine halves on the bulgur, drizzle with the tahini sauce and scatter with the pomegranate seeds.

recipes.title: Baked beef kofta in spiced tomato sauce
recipes.blurb: Soft cumin-scented beef meatballs simmered in a smoky tomato sauce with pepper, served on buttery rice.
steps: Mix the beef with the grated onion, half the garlic, the cumin, coriander, paprika, cinnamon, half the parsley, half the salt and the pepper. Shape into 12 small ovals.
Heat the oil in a wide ovenproof pan over a medium-high heat and brown the koftas for 4 minutes, turning. Lift out onto a plate.
Add the diced onion and red pepper to the pan and cook for 6 minutes. Stir in the remaining garlic and tomato puree for 1 minute, then add the chopped tomatoes and remaining salt.
Nestle the koftas back into the sauce, cover and simmer gently for 12 minutes until cooked through and the sauce is thick.
While they simmer, boil the rice in salted water for 10 minutes and drain.
Spoon the koftas and sauce over the rice and scatter with the remaining parsley.

recipes.title: Lentil and rice mujaddara with crispy onions
recipes.blurb: Comforting cumin-scented lentils and rice topped with deeply browned onions and a cool yoghurt and cucumber side.
steps: Heat 30 ml of the oil in a wide pan over a medium heat, add the onions with a pinch of salt and cook for 20 minutes, stirring often, until deep brown and crisp at the edges. Lift out half onto a plate.
Add the remaining oil to the pan with the cumin seeds, ground cumin and cinnamon and stir for 30 seconds.
Add the rinsed rice and stir to coat, then pour in 300 ml of boiling water mixed with the stock cube. Cover and cook on a low heat for 10 minutes.
Stir in the lentils, cover again and cook for 5 minutes more until the rice is tender and the liquid has been absorbed. Season with salt, pepper and a squeeze of lemon.
Mix the yoghurt with the cucumber, mint and a pinch of salt.
Serve the rice and lentils topped with the crispy onions and the yoghurt alongside.

recipes.title: Chicken tagine with dates and olives
recipes.blurb: Slow-simmered chicken in ginger, cinnamon and saffron-style turmeric with sweet dates and briny olives, over couscous.
steps: Season the chicken with salt and pepper. Heat the oil in a lidded casserole or deep pan over a medium-high heat and brown the chicken for 3 minutes per side, then set aside.
Lower the heat and cook the onion and carrot for 6 minutes. Add the garlic, ginger, cinnamon, turmeric and cumin and stir for 1 minute.
Return the chicken, add the tomatoes and the stock cube dissolved in 200 ml of hot water. Cover and simmer for 25 minutes until the chicken is very tender.
Stir in the dates and olives and cook uncovered for 5 minutes until the sauce is rich and glossy.
Meanwhile, pour 150 ml of boiling water over the couscous with a pinch of salt, cover for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork and stir in the lemon zest.
Finish the tagine with lemon juice and coriander and serve on the couscous with the almonds scattered over.

recipes.title: Harissa king prawns with lemon couscous
recipes.blurb: Prawns tossed in rose harissa and seared fast, over lemony herb couscous with roasted peppers.
steps: Toss the prawns with the harissa, garlic, 10 ml of the oil and a pinch of salt and leave for 5 minutes.
Put the couscous in a bowl, pour over 150 ml of boiling water mixed with the stock cube, cover and leave for 5 minutes.
Fluff the couscous with a fork and stir through the roasted peppers, spring onions, parsley, mint, the remaining oil, the zest of the lemon and a squeeze of juice.
Heat a large frying pan until very hot and cook the prawns for 2 to 3 minutes, turning once, until pink and lightly charred.
Pile the couscous onto plates, top with the prawns and add a spoonful of yoghurt loosened with a squeeze of lemon.

recipes.title: Butternut and chickpea tagine with raisin couscous
recipes.blurb: Gently spiced squash and chickpeas stewed in tomato with raisins, served over fluffy couscous.
steps: Heat the oil in a large lidded pan and cook the onion for 6 minutes until soft. Add the garlic, ras el hanout, cumin and cinnamon and stir for 1 minute.
Add the squash, tomatoes, raisins, stock cube dissolved in 150 ml of hot water, salt and pepper. Bring to a simmer, cover and cook for 20 minutes.
Stir in the chickpeas and cook uncovered for 8 to 10 minutes until the squash is tender and the sauce has thickened.
Meanwhile, pour 150 ml of boiling water over the couscous with a pinch of salt, cover for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
Fold the spinach through the tagine until wilted, add lemon juice to taste and stir in most of the coriander.
Serve over the couscous with the rest of the coriander on top.

recipes.title: Fiery harissa lamb meatballs
recipes.blurb: Spiced lamb meatballs in a hot harissa and chilli tomato sauce, with couscous and a cooling yoghurt spoonful.
steps: Mix the lamb with the grated onion, half the garlic, 15 g of the harissa, the cumin, coriander, half the salt and the chilli flakes. Shape into 12 meatballs.
Heat the oil in a wide, lidded pan and brown the meatballs for 5 minutes, turning. Take them out and set aside.
In the same pan, cook the diced onion for 5 minutes, then add the remaining garlic, the red chilli and the rest of the harissa and stir for 1 minute.
