Meanwhile, boil the penne in well-salted water for 10-11 minutes until al dente, then drain.
Taste the sauce for seasoning, scatter with parsley and serve over the penne.

recipes.title: Sausage and broccoli fusilli, orecchiette-style
recipes.blurb: Garlicky sausage nuggets and broccoli cooked down until it clings to the pasta in a lemony, chilli-warm sauce.

ingredients.name: Broccoli
ingredients.prep: cut into small florets, stalk diced

steps: Bring a large pan of well-salted water to the boil. Add the fusilli and cook for 10-11 minutes, dropping in the broccoli for the final 4 minutes. Reserve a mugful of the water, then drain.

While the pasta cooks, heat half the oil in a large frying pan over a medium-high heat. Pinch the sausage meat into small nuggets and fry for 7-8 minutes, turning, until deeply browned and cooked through.
Turn the heat down, add the garlic and chilli flakes and cook for 1 minute until fragrant but not coloured.

Tip in the drained pasta and broccoli with the remaining oil, a ladleful of the reserved water, the zest of the lemon and most of the parmesan. Toss over the heat for 1-2 minutes, crushing some of the broccoli, until the sauce turns glossy.
Squeeze in a little lemon juice, season with pepper and serve with the rest of the parmesan on top.

recipes.title: Sicilian aubergine caponata with soft polenta
recipes.blurb: Sweet-sour aubergine, celery, capers and olives piled over creamy polenta, with toasted pine nuts on top.
steps: Heat 30 ml of the oil in a large frying pan over a medium-high heat. Fry the aubergine with a pinch of salt for 10-12 minutes, stirring often, until golden and soft. Tip onto a plate.
In the same pan, cook the celery and onion in the remaining oil for 6 minutes until softened, then add the garlic for 30 seconds.
Return the aubergine with the cherry tomatoes, vinegar, sugar, capers and olives. Simmer for 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until the tomatoes collapse and the sauce is glossy and sweet-sour.
Meanwhile, toast the pine nuts in a dry pan for 2 minutes until golden, shaking often, and set aside.

Bring 600 ml of water to the boil with the remaining salt. Pour in the polenta in a steady stream, whisking, then cook over a low heat for 5-8 minutes, stirring, until thick and creamy. Season with pepper.
Spoon the polenta into bowls, top with the caponata, then the pine nuts and basil. It is just as good warm or at room temperature.

recipes.title: Salmon puttanesca spaghetti
recipes.blurb: Salmon fillets poached in a briny tomato, olive and caper sauce, flaked over spaghetti.
steps: Boil the spaghetti in a large pan of well-salted water for 9-10 minutes until al dente. Reserve a mugful of the cooking water, then drain.

Meanwhile, warm the oil in a deep frying pan over a medium heat. Cook the garlic and chilli flakes for 1 minute, then add the chopped tomatoes, olives and capers. Simmer for 6 minutes until slightly thickened.
Season the salmon lightly with pepper and nestle the fillets into the sauce. Cover and cook gently for 7-8 minutes, until the salmon is just cooked through.
Lift the salmon onto a plate and break it into large flakes. Toss the spaghetti through the sauce with a splash of the reserved water until coated.
Fold the salmon back in very gently, check the seasoning (the olives and capers are already salty) and scatter with parsley.

recipes.title: Mushroom and spinach lasagne
recipes.blurb: Garlicky mushrooms, spinach, tomato and creamy ricotta layered between pasta sheets under a bubbling mozzarella lid.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Warm the oil in a large pan over a high heat and fry the mushrooms for 7-8 minutes until deeply golden and dry. Add the onion and cook for 4 minutes, then the garlic and oregano for 30 seconds.
Pour in the chopped tomatoes with a pinch of salt and pepper and simmer for 8 minutes. Stir in the spinach a handful at a time until wilted, and take off the heat.
Beat the ricotta with half the parmesan, a pinch of salt and a splash of water until smooth and spreadable.
In a small baking dish, spoon a layer of the mushroom sauce, then a layer of pasta sheets, then dollops of ricotta. Repeat twice more, finishing with sauce.
Top with the mozzarella and remaining parmesan. Cover with foil and bake for 20 minutes, then uncover and bake for 12-15 minutes more until golden and bubbling.
Rest for 5 minutes before cutting so the layers hold together.

recipes.title: Risotto primavera with lemon and mint
recipes.blurb: Creamy risotto studded with courgette, asparagus and peas, brightened with lemon zest and fresh mint.

ingredients.name: Asparagus
ingredients.prep: woody ends snapped off, cut into 3 cm pieces

steps: Dissolve the stock cubes in 900 ml of boiling water and keep it hot in a pan on the back of the hob.

Heat the oil in a wide, heavy pan over a medium heat. Cook the shallot and courgette with a pinch of salt for 5 minutes until soft, then stir in the garlic and rice and toast for 1-2 minutes until the grains look glassy.
Pour in the white wine and stir until it has almost all been absorbed, about 2 minutes.
Add the stock a ladleful at a time, stirring often and letting each addition absorb before adding the next. After 10 minutes, add the asparagus.
Keep adding stock for another 6-8 minutes until the rice is tender with a little bite, adding the peas for the final 3 minutes. You may not need all the stock.
Take off the heat and beat in the butter, parmesan, lemon zest and a squeeze of juice. Cover for 2 minutes, then loosen with a splash of stock so it flows slowly across the plate.
Season to taste and top with the mint and plenty of black pepper.

recipes.title: Pasta alla norma with ricotta and basil
recipes.blurb: Roasted aubergine in a rich tomato sauce tossed with rigatoni, topped with cool ricotta and torn basil.
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Toss the aubergine on a large tray with 30 ml of the oil and half the salt. Roast for 25 minutes, turning once, until golden and creamy inside.
Meanwhile, warm the remaining oil in a pan over a medium heat. Cook the garlic and chilli flakes for 1 minute, add the chopped tomatoes and simmer for 15 minutes until thick and jammy.
Boil the rigatoni in well-salted water for 11-12 minutes until al dente. Reserve a mugful of water and drain.
Stir the roasted aubergine into the sauce, add the pasta and a splash of the cooking water and toss over the heat for 1 minute.
Season with pepper and serve topped with spoonfuls of ricotta and the basil.

recipes.title: Chicken saltimbocca with sage, ham and lemon
recipes.blurb: Thin chicken escalopes wrapped in ham and sage, crisped in butter, with a lemon and white wine pan sauce and buttery potatoes.

ingredients.name: Chicken breast
ingredients.prep: 2 breasts, sliced in half horizontally and flattened

steps: Put the potatoes in a pan of well-salted cold water, bring to the boil and simmer for 12 minutes, adding the green beans for the final 4 minutes. Drain well.
Season the chicken with salt and pepper. Press 2 sage leaves onto each piece, then lay a slice of ham over them, pressing so it sticks. Dust very lightly with flour.

Heat the oil in a large frying pan over a medium-high heat. Fry the chicken ham-side down for 3 minutes until the ham is crisp, flip and cook for 2-3 minutes more until cooked through. Move to a plate and keep warm.
Add the butter to the pan with the potatoes and cook for 4-5 minutes until golden at the edges. Tip the potatoes and beans into a bowl.

Pour the wine and the juice of half the lemon into the pan, scraping up the bits, and bubble for 2 minutes until reduced by half. Add 40 ml of water and bubble for 1 minute more. Spoon over the chicken and serve with the potatoes, beans and a wedge of the remaining lemon.

recipes.title: Gnocchi with sage brown butter, squash and walnuts
recipes.blurb: Pan-crisped gnocchi and roasted butternut in nutty sage brown butter, scattered with walnuts and parmesan.

ingredients.name: Butternut squash
ingredients.prep: peeled and cut into 2 cm cubes

steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Toss the squash on a tray with the oil and a good pinch of salt and pepper. Roast for 25 minutes, turning once, until soft and caramelised at the edges.
Bring a pan of salted water to the boil. Cook the gnocchi for 2-3 minutes until they float, then drain well.

Melt the butter in a large frying pan over a medium heat. Once it foams and smells nutty, after about 3 minutes, add the sage leaves and fry for 30 seconds until crisp, then lift them out. Add the gnocchi and fry for 4-5 minutes, turning, until golden and crisp in places.
Add the garlic and walnuts for 1 minute, then fold in the spinach until just wilted.
Gently stir through the roasted squash, check the seasoning and serve scattered with the crisp sage and the parmesan.

recipes.title: Quick minestrone with white beans
recipes.blurb: A fast, veg-packed tomato soup with small pasta, white beans and a handful of greens.
steps: Warm the oil in a large pot over a medium heat. Cook the onion, carrot and celery with a pinch of salt for 6 minutes until beginning to soften.
Add the courgette, garlic and tomato puree and stir for 2 minutes.
Pour in the chopped tomatoes and 800 ml of boiling water, crumble in the stock cube and add the beans. Bring to a simmer and cook for 8 minutes.
Stir in the pasta and simmer for 8-10 minutes until just tender, adding a splash more water if the soup gets too thick.
Fold in the spinach until wilted, season well with salt and pepper, and serve with the basil on top.

recipes.title: Chicken souvlaki plates with tzatziki and pittas
recipes.blurb: Lemon-oregano chicken seared until charred, piled with tzatziki, tomato and red onion on warm pittas.
steps: Mix the chicken in a bowl with the oregano, 2 of the garlic cloves, the zest and juice of half the lemon, 20 ml of the oil, and a good pinch of salt and pepper. Leave for 15 minutes while you prepare everything else.
For the tzatziki, coarsely grate half the cucumber and squeeze out as much water as you can. Stir into the yoghurt with the last garlic clove and a pinch of salt.
Slice the remaining cucumber and toss with the tomatoes, red onion, the remaining oil and a squeeze of lemon juice. Season well.
Heat a large frying pan or griddle over a high heat. Cook the chicken in a single layer for 8-10 minutes, turning, until charred in places and cooked through.
Warm the pittas in a dry pan or the toaster for 1 minute.
Serve the chicken on plates with the pittas, salad and tzatziki, with lemon wedges from the remaining half.

recipes.title: Gemista (herby rice stuffed tomatoes and peppers)
recipes.blurb: Sweet tomatoes and peppers baked with a mint-and-parsley rice filling and golden potatoes alongside.
steps: Heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan). Slice the tops off the tomatoes and keep them as lids. Scoop the pulp into a bowl and chop it roughly, discarding any hard core. Set the hollowed tomatoes and pepper halves in a snug baking dish.
Warm 15 ml of the oil in a pan over a medium heat and cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft. Stir in the garlic for 30 seconds, then take off the heat.

Mix the onion with the tomato pulp, rice, parsley, mint, tomato puree, a good pinch of salt and pepper, and 15 ml of the oil. Spoon into the tomatoes and peppers, filling them only about three-quarters full to leave room for the rice to swell.
Put the tomato lids back on. Tuck the potatoes around the vegetables, pour 150 ml of water into the dish, and drizzle everything with the remaining oil and a sprinkle of salt.
Cover tightly with foil and bake for 30 minutes, then remove the foil and bake for another 25-30 minutes until the rice is tender and the tops and potatoes are golden.
Rest for 5 minutes and serve warm with the juices spooned over.

recipes.title: Fasolakia (Greek green bean and potato stew)
recipes.blurb: Green beans and potatoes slowly simmered in olive oil and tomato until silky, with fresh dill to finish.
steps: Warm 30 ml of the oil in a wide, deep pan over a medium heat. Cook the onion for 6 minutes until soft and golden, adding the garlic for the last minute.
Add the potatoes and stir for 2 minutes so they pick up some of the oil.
Tip in the chopped tomatoes, sugar, salt, pepper and 200 ml of water. Stir in the green beans and bring to a simmer.

Cover and cook over a low heat for 25-30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the beans are completely soft and the sauce has reduced to a rich, oily gravy. Add a splash of water if it starts to catch.
Stir through the parsley and half the dill. Serve warm, scattered with the remaining dill and the remaining oil trickled over, with the bread alongside to mop up the sauce.

recipes.title: Prawn saganaki with feta and warm pittas
recipes.blurb: Juicy prawns simmered in a garlicky tomato and white wine sauce, topped with melting feta and mopped up with warm pittas.
steps: Heat the oil in a deep frying pan over a medium heat. Cook the onion with a pinch of salt for 5 minutes until soft, then add the garlic, chilli and oregano for 1 minute.

Pour in the white wine and let it bubble for 1-2 minutes, then add the chopped tomatoes and the juice of half the lemon. Simmer for 8-10 minutes until the sauce is thick and glossy, seasoning with salt and pepper.
Stir in the prawns and cook for 3-4 minutes, turning once, until pink and just cooked through.
Scatter the feta over the top, cover with a lid or a baking tray for 2 minutes until it softens, or finish under a hot grill for 2 minutes until lightly golden.
Warm the pittas in a dry pan or the toaster. Scatter the parsley over the saganaki and serve with the pittas and lemon wedges.

recipes.title: Catalan-style chickpeas with spinach, raisins and pine nuts
recipes.blurb: Garlicky chickpeas and wilted spinach with sweet raisins, toasted pine nuts and smoked paprika, with fried bread.
steps: Heat 10 ml of the oil in a large frying pan over a medium heat. Toast the pine nuts for 1-2 minutes until golden, shaking constantly, and tip onto a plate.

Add 20 ml more oil with the onion and cook for 5 minutes until soft. Stir in the garlic and smoked paprika for 30 seconds, then add the chickpeas and raisins and cook for 5 minutes, crushing a few chickpeas, until the edges colour.
Add the spinach in handfuls, stirring until wilted, then splash in the vinegar and season with salt and pepper. Cook for 1-2 minutes until the liquid has mostly evaporated.
In a separate pan, fry the bread in the remaining oil for 1-2 minutes a side until golden and crisp.
Spoon the chickpeas over the fried bread and scatter with the pine nuts.

recipes.title: Albóndigas in smoky tomato sauce with potatoes
recipes.blurb: Tender beef and pork meatballs simmered in smoky tomato and pepper sauce, with buttery boiled potatoes.
steps: Boil the potatoes in well-salted water for 12-15 minutes until tender, then drain and keep warm.

In a bowl, combine both minces with the panko, egg, half the onion, the crushed garlic, parsley, 2 g of the paprika, the cumin, half the salt and plenty of pepper. Mix well and roll into 14-16 small balls.
Heat half the oil in a deep frying pan over a medium-high heat. Brown the meatballs for 6-8 minutes, turning, then transfer to a plate.
Add the remaining oil, the rest of the onion and the red pepper to the pan and cook for 6 minutes. Add the sliced garlic and the rest of the paprika for 30 seconds.

Pour in the chopped tomatoes and 100 ml of water and simmer for 5 minutes. Return the meatballs and add the peas, then cover and cook gently for 10 minutes until the meatballs are cooked through and the sauce is rich.
Season to taste with the remaining salt and serve over or alongside the potatoes.

recipes.title: Pisto with fried eggs and toast
recipes.blurb: A slow-cooked Spanish vegetable stew of courgette, peppers and tomato, crowned with crisp-edged fried eggs.
steps: Heat 30 ml of the oil in a large, deep pan over a medium heat. Cook the onion, red pepper and green pepper with a pinch of salt for 10 minutes until soft and sweet.
Add the courgette, garlic and smoked paprika and cook for 5 minutes, stirring, until the courgette starts to soften.
Pour in the chopped tomatoes and sugar and simmer over a low heat for 12-15 minutes until the vegetables are tender and the sauce is thick and jammy. Season well with salt and pepper.

While the pisto finishes, toast the bread. Heat the remaining oil in a frying pan over a medium-high heat and fry the eggs for 2-3 minutes until the whites are crisp at the edges and the yolks still runny.
Spoon the pisto onto plates, top with the fried eggs and parsley, and serve with the toast.

recipes.title: Garlic prawns with crispy patatas
recipes.blurb: Sizzling prawns in garlic, chilli and smoked paprika oil, spooned over golden crisp potatoes with lemon.
steps: Boil the potatoes in well-salted water for 10-12 minutes until just tender, then drain and let them steam dry for 2 minutes.

Heat 30 ml of the oil in a large frying pan over a medium-high heat. Fry the potatoes cut-side down for 8-10 minutes without moving them too much, until deep golden and crisp, then season with salt and tip into a bowl.
Wipe out the pan and add the remaining oil with the garlic and chilli over a medium heat. Cook for 1-2 minutes, until the garlic just starts to turn pale gold.
Add the paprika and the prawns with a pinch of salt and cook for 2-3 minutes, turning once, until pink and curled.
Pile the potatoes onto plates, spoon over the prawns and all the garlicky oil, then scatter with parsley and pepper and serve with the lemon wedges.

recipes.title: Fabada-style bean stew with chorizo and kale
recipes.blurb: White beans simmered with smoky chorizo, bacon and paprika into a thick Asturian-style stew, finished with kale.
steps: Heat the oil in a large, heavy pot over a medium heat. Fry the chorizo and lardons for 5-6 minutes until the fat runs and they turn golden. Lift out with a slotted spoon, leaving the fat in the pot.
Cook the onion and carrot in the fat for 8 minutes until soft, then stir in the garlic and smoked paprika for 30 seconds.
Add the beans, bay leaves and the stock cube dissolved in 500 ml of boiling water. Return the chorizo and lardons, bring to a simmer and cook gently, partly covered, for 20 minutes.
Crush a few spoonfuls of the beans against the side of the pot to thicken the broth. Stir in the kale and simmer for 5-6 minutes until tender.
Remove the bay leaves, season with the salt and plenty of pepper and serve in deep bowls. The stew thickens as it stands and is even better the next day.

recipes.title: Chicken tinga tostadas with lime crema
recipes.blurb: Smoky chipotle-tomato chicken piled onto crisp-baked corn tortillas with cool lime soured cream.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Brush the tortillas on both sides with half the oil, lay them on two trays and bake for 8–10 minutes, turning once, until stiff and golden.

Meanwhile, heat the remaining oil in a wide frying pan over a medium heat and fry the onion with a pinch of salt for 6 minutes until soft. Stir in the garlic, chipotle paste, smoked paprika and oregano for 1 minute.
Add the grated tomato, the chicken and 100 ml of water. Simmer, stirring now and then, for 12–15 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and the sauce is thick and clinging.
Shred the chicken roughly in the pan with two forks, then season with salt and pepper.
Stir half the lime juice and a pinch of salt into the soured cream. Toss the cabbage with the rest of the juice, and mash the avocado with a pinch of salt.
Spread each tostada with avocado, pile on the chicken and cabbage, then finish with lime cream and coriander.

recipes.title: Carnitas-style pork with orange and pickled onion
recipes.blurb: Pork simmered in orange and spices, then crisped in the pan and tucked into corn tortillas.
steps: Toss the red onion with the juice of the lime and a pinch of salt in a small bowl, and leave it to soften and turn pink.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over a high heat and brown the pork in a single layer for 5 minutes, turning, then season with salt and pepper.

Add the onion wedges, garlic, cumin, oregano, bay leaf, the juice of the orange and 3 strips of its zest, then pour in 150 ml of water. Cover loosely and simmer on a low heat for 35–40 minutes until the pork is very tender.
Remove the lid, discard the bay leaf and zest and turn the heat up. Boil off the liquid, then fry the pork for 4–5 minutes, breaking it up, until the edges are crisp and caramelised.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan for 30 seconds each side and fill with pork, pickled onion, radish and coriander.

recipes.title: Chicken enchiladas suizas-style
recipes.blurb: Rolled corn tortillas filled with chicken, baked under a creamy green jalapeño sauce and melted cheddar.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Melt the butter in a frying pan over a medium heat and fry the onion for 5 minutes, then add the chicken and garlic and cook for 6–7 minutes until the chicken is cooked through.

Scoop half the chicken mixture into a bowl. Stir the flour into the pan for 1 minute, then pour in the milk and 150 ml of water with the stock cube crumbled in, stirring until smooth. Simmer for 4 minutes until thickened.
Off the heat, stir in the jalapeños, soured cream, most of the coriander and a squeeze of lime. Season with salt and pepper.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan for 20 seconds each side so they bend without cracking. Fill each with chicken and a little cheddar, roll up and lay seam-side down in a baking dish.
Pour the sauce over the enchiladas, scatter with the remaining cheddar and bake for 15–18 minutes until bubbling and golden. Top with the rest of the coriander and lime wedges.

recipes.title: Chiles rellenos-style stuffed peppers
recipes.blurb: Green peppers roasted until soft, filled with melting cheese and corn and served in a smoky tomato sauce.
steps: Heat the oven to 210°C (190°C fan). Rub the pepper halves with half the oil and a pinch of salt, set them cut-side up in a baking dish and roast for 15 minutes until starting to soften.
Mix the mozzarella, cheddar, sweetcorn, spring onions, jalapeños and half the coriander in a bowl, and season with pepper.
Warm the remaining oil in a small pan over a medium heat and fry the garlic and cumin for 30 seconds, then add the passata and a pinch of salt and simmer for 8 minutes until slightly thickened.
Spoon the cheese filling into the peppers, pour the sauce around them and roast for another 12–15 minutes until the cheese is bubbling and golden.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan or the oven for a minute. Serve the peppers with the sauce spooned over, scattered with the rest of the coriander, with the tortillas alongside.

recipes.title: Smoky black bean tortilla soup
recipes.blurb: A chipotle tomato soup with black beans, topped with crushed tortilla chips, avocado and lime.
steps: Heat the oil in a large pan over a medium heat and fry the onion and red pepper with a pinch of salt for 8 minutes until soft.
Stir in the garlic, chipotle paste and cumin and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the tin of tomatoes, the beans, the stock cube and 500 ml of water. Bring to the boil, then simmer for 12 minutes.
Use a stick blender to blitz about a third of the soup so it thickens but stays chunky, then season with salt, pepper and half the lime juice.
Ladle into bowls and top with crushed tortilla chips, avocado, coriander and lime wedges.

recipes.title: Chipotle chilaquiles with fried eggs
recipes.blurb: Crisp tortilla chips simmered briefly in smoky red sauce, topped with runny eggs, feta and cream.

ingredients.name: Red onion
ingredients.prep: half finely diced, half thinly sliced

steps: Heat half the oil in a large frying pan over a medium heat and fry the diced onion for 4 minutes, then add the garlic and chipotle paste and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in the passata and 100 ml of water, add the beans and the salt, and simmer for 5 minutes until the sauce is thick and glossy.
Fold the tortilla chips through the sauce for 1–2 minutes only, until just coated and starting to soften at the edges but still with some bite.
While the tortilla chips cook, heat the remaining oil in a second pan over a medium-high heat and fry the eggs for 2–3 minutes until the whites are set and the yolks still runny. Season with pepper.
Divide the chilaquiles between plates and top with the eggs, feta, soured cream, avocado, sliced red onion, chilli and coriander, with lime wedges to squeeze over.

recipes.title: Baja-style crispy fish tacos with lime slaw
recipes.blurb: Panko-crusted white fish in corn tortillas with crunchy cabbage slaw and a spiced lime cream.
steps: Mix the cabbage with half the lime juice, half the coriander and a pinch of salt. In a small bowl, stir the mayonnaise, soured cream, hot sauce and the rest of the lime juice together.
Mix the flour with the chilli powder, smoked paprika, 2 teaspoons of salt and the pepper on a plate. Put the egg in a shallow bowl and the panko on another plate.
Dredge each piece of fish in the flour, dip in the egg, then press into the panko to coat all over.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan over a medium-high heat. Fry the fish in two batches for 2–3 minutes per side until deep golden and cooked through, then drain on kitchen paper.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan for 30 seconds each side. Fill with slaw and fish, drizzle with the lime cream and finish with the remaining coriander.

recipes.title: Sopa de lima-style chicken soup
recipes.blurb: A bright, limey chicken and tomato broth with green pepper and crisp tortilla chips on top.
steps: Heat the oil in a large pan over a medium heat and fry the onion and green pepper for 6 minutes until softened.
Stir in the garlic, oregano and cumin for 1 minute, then add the tomatoes and cook for 3 minutes until they begin to break down.
Crumble in the stock cube, add 700 ml of water and the whole chicken breasts, then bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for 14–16 minutes until the chicken is cooked through.
Lift the chicken out, shred it with two forks and return it to the pan. Stir in the juice of 1 lime and the zest of half, then season with salt and pepper.
Ladle into bowls and top with crushed tortilla chips, coriander and wedges cut from the second lime.

recipes.title: Tlayuda-style black bean and avocado flatbreads
recipes.blurb: Crisp-baked tortillas spread with garlicky black beans, then heaped with cabbage, avocado and radish.
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Brush the tortillas with half the oil, lay them on trays and bake for 5 minutes until just starting to crisp.

Meanwhile, warm the remaining oil in a small pan over a medium heat and fry the garlic and cumin for 30 seconds. Add the beans with 50 ml of water and mash roughly with a fork, cooking for 3 minutes until thick and spreadable. Season with salt, pepper and half the hot sauce.
Spread the beans over the tortillas and return them to the oven for 5–6 minutes until the edges are crisp and golden.
Toss the cabbage and radish with the juice of the lime and a pinch of salt.
Top the flatbreads with the cabbage mix, avocado and coriander, then drizzle with the rest of the hot sauce.

recipes.title: Mushroom barbacoa-style tacos
recipes.blurb: Torn mushrooms slow-fried in chipotle and spices, piled into corn tortillas with avocado and pickled onion.
steps: Toss the red onion with half the lime juice and a pinch of salt and leave to pickle while you cook.

Heat the oil in a large frying pan over a high heat and fry the mushrooms in a single layer, undisturbed for 3 minutes, then stir and cook for another 8 minutes until deeply browned and the moisture has gone.
Add the garlic, chipotle paste, tomato puree, soy sauce, cumin, smoked paprika and oregano with 80 ml of water. Cook for 4–5 minutes, stirring, until sticky and almost dry. Season with pepper.
Mash the avocado with the rest of the lime juice and a pinch of salt.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan for 30 seconds each side, then fill with avocado, mushrooms, pickled onion and coriander.

recipes.title: Al pastor-style pork and pineapple tacos
recipes.blurb: Thin pork marinated in chilli and vinegar, seared hot with charred pineapple and served on corn tortillas.

ingredients.name: Pineapple chunks (tin)
ingredients.prep: drained and cut into small chunks

steps: Mix the chilli powder, paprika, cumin, oregano, garlic, vinegar, salt and pepper in a bowl, add the pork and turn to coat. Leave for 10 minutes.
Heat a large frying pan over a high heat until very hot. Add the pineapple and cook for 3–4 minutes without moving it until charred at the edges, then tip onto a plate.
Add the oil to the pan and fry the pork in two batches for 2–3 minutes per batch until browned and slightly crisp at the edges.
Mix the diced onion, coriander and the juice of half the lime with a pinch of salt for a quick topping.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan for 30 seconds each side and fill with pork, pineapple and the onion mix, with the remaining lime cut into wedges.

recipes.title: Elote-style corn rice bowl with black beans
recipes.blurb: Charred corn in a tangy, creamy, chilli-dusted dressing over rice with black beans and feta.
steps: Cook the rice in plenty of boiling salted water for 10–12 minutes until tender, drain well and keep covered.
Rub the corn cobs with the oil and cook in a hot dry or lightly oiled pan for 10–12 minutes, turning, until charred in places. Stand each cob upright and slice off the kernels.
Stir the soured cream, mayonnaise, juice of half the lime, half the chilli powder and a pinch of salt together to make the dressing.
Warm the beans in a small pan with the smoked paprika, the remaining chilli powder and a splash of water for 3 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.
Divide the rice between bowls and top with beans and corn, then drizzle over the dressing and scatter with feta, spring onions, coriander and lime wedges.

recipes.title: Carne asada-style steak with charred spring onions
recipes.blurb: Lime and cumin marinated steak, seared and sliced with charred spring onions, tomato salsa and warm tortillas.
steps: Rub the steak with half the oil, the juice of 1 lime, the garlic, cumin, chilli powder, soy sauce and pepper. Leave for 10–15 minutes while you make the salsa.
For the salsa, mix the tomatoes, the diced red onion, most of the coriander, the juice of half the second lime and a good pinch of salt.
Heat a heavy frying pan over a high heat until smoking. Cook the steak for 3–4 minutes per side for medium, then rest on a board for 5 minutes.
In the same pan with the remaining oil, char the spring onions for 3–4 minutes, turning, until blackened in spots.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan for 30 seconds each side. Slice the steak thinly across the grain and serve with the spring onions, salsa, avocado, tortillas and the remaining lime in wedges.

recipes.title: Mexican-style prawn and tomato rice
recipes.blurb: Fluffy rice cooked in smoky tomato with sweet peppers and peas, topped with seared garlic prawns.
steps: Heat half the oil in a lidded frying pan over a medium heat and fry the onion and red pepper for 6 minutes. Add half the garlic, the chipotle paste and cumin and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the rice to coat it, then add the passata, the stock cube and 300 ml of water. Bring to the boil, cover and cook on the lowest heat for 12 minutes.
Scatter the peas over the rice, cover again and cook for 3 minutes, then turn off the heat and leave it covered for 5 minutes.
While the rice rests, heat the remaining oil in a second pan over a high heat and cook the prawns with the remaining garlic, salt and pepper for 2–3 minutes until pink and curled.
Fluff the rice with a fork, top with the prawns, squeeze over lime juice and finish with coriander.

recipes.title: Smoky pepper and bean burrito bowls with lime rice
recipes.blurb: Spiced roasted peppers, black beans and sweetcorn over lime rice with a quick tomato salsa and avocado.

ingredients.name: Red onion
ingredients.prep: half cut into wedges, half finely diced

steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Toss the red pepper, onion wedges and sweetcorn on a tray with half the oil, the cumin, smoked paprika, salt and pepper. Roast for 20–25 minutes until charred at the edges.
Cook the rice in boiling salted water for 10–12 minutes, drain and stir through the zest and juice of 1 lime and half the coriander.
Stir the beans into the tray for the last 5 minutes to warm through.
Mix the tomatoes, diced onion, jalapeños, the juice of half the second lime, the remaining oil and a pinch of salt for the salsa.
Spoon the rice into bowls and top with the roasted vegetables and beans, the salsa, avocado, the remaining coriander and a wedge of lime.

recipes.title: Chorizo and crispy potato tacos
recipes.blurb: Paprika-red chorizo and golden diced potato in warm corn tortillas with lime soured cream and hot sauce.
steps: Boil the potato in salted water for 5 minutes until just tender, then drain well and let it steam dry for 2 minutes.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan over a medium heat, add the chorizo and fry for 3–4 minutes until it releases its red oil, then lift it out with a slotted spoon.

Add the potato to the chorizo oil and fry on a medium-high heat for 8–10 minutes, turning only now and then, until golden and crisp. Add the onion for the last 4 minutes, and the garlic for the final minute.
Return the chorizo to the pan, season with pepper and a pinch of salt if needed, and stir through the hot sauce.
Mix the soured cream with the juice of half the lime. Warm the tortillas in a dry pan for 30 seconds each side, fill with the chorizo mix, and top with the lime cream, coriander and lime wedges.

recipes.title: Mole-style sweet potato and chickpea stew
recipes.blurb: Sweet potato and chickpeas in a rich, nutty chipotle and cinnamon sauce, spooned over rice.

ingredients.name: Sweet potato
ingredients.prep: peeled and cut into 2 cm cubes

steps: Heat the oil in a large pan over a medium heat and fry the onion for 6 minutes until soft, then stir in the garlic, chipotle paste, cinnamon and cumin for 1 minute.
Add the chopped tomatoes, peanut butter, the stock cube and 250 ml of water, stirring until the peanut butter dissolves into the sauce.
Add the sweet potato, bring to a simmer and cook, partly covered, for 15 minutes until almost tender. Stir in the chickpeas and cook for another 6–8 minutes until the sauce is thick.
Meanwhile, cook the rice in boiling salted water for 10–12 minutes and drain well.
Season the stew with salt and pepper, serve over the rice, and scatter with toasted sesame seeds and coriander.

recipes.title: Lomo saltado-style beef with potato wedges and rice
recipes.blurb: Peruvian-style stir-fried steak, onion and tomato in a soy and vinegar sizzle, with roast wedges and rice.
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Toss the potato wedges on a tray with 15 ml of the oil, the cumin, salt and pepper and roast for 30–35 minutes, turning halfway, until crisp and golden.
Cook the rice in boiling salted water for 10–12 minutes, then drain and keep warm.

Mix the soy sauce and vinegar in a small bowl. Heat 15 ml of the oil in a wok or large frying pan over the highest heat until smoking and sear the beef in two batches for 1–2 minutes each, then set aside.
Add the remaining oil, the onion and chilli and stir-fry for 2 minutes. Add the garlic and tomatoes and toss for 1 minute.
Return the beef to the pan, pour over the soy and vinegar and toss for 30 seconds until sizzling and glossy. Serve over the rice with the wedges alongside, scattered with coriander.

recipes.title: Feijoada-style black bean and chorizo stew
recipes.blurb: A smoky Brazilian-style black bean stew with chorizo and bacon, with orange wedges, kale and rice.
steps: Heat the oil in a large pan over a medium heat and fry the bacon and chorizo for 5 minutes until they release their fat and start to crisp.
Add the onion and green pepper and cook for 6 minutes until soft, then stir in the garlic and smoked paprika for 1 minute.
Add the beans, bay leaves, the stock cube and 300 ml of water, then simmer uncovered for 20–25 minutes, mashing a few beans against the side of the pan, until thick and glossy.
Meanwhile, cook the rice in boiling salted water for 10–12 minutes and drain well.
Stir the kale into the stew for the last 3 minutes. Squeeze in the juice of half the orange, season with salt and pepper and discard the bay leaves.
Serve the stew over the rice with the remaining orange cut into wedges.

recipes.title: Moqueca-style coconut fish stew
recipes.blurb: White fish poached in a fragrant coconut, tomato and pepper broth, served with rice and lime.
steps: Heat the oil in a wide pan over a medium heat and fry the onion and both peppers (red pepper and yellow pepper) for 6 minutes until starting to soften.
Stir in the garlic, chilli and paprika for 1 minute, then add the tomatoes and cook for 3 minutes until they break down.
Pour in the coconut milk with 100 ml of water and half the lime juice, and simmer gently for 8 minutes.
Meanwhile, cook the rice in boiling salted water for 10–12 minutes and drain.
Season the fish with salt and pepper and nestle it into the broth. Cover and cook on a low heat for 5–6 minutes until just opaque and flaking.
Spoon the stew over the rice, scatter with coriander and serve with the rest of the lime in wedges.

recipes.title: Colombian-style red beans and rice with avocado
recipes.blurb: Tender red beans in a sofrito of tomato, carrot and spring onion, spooned over rice with creamy avocado.
steps: Heat half the oil in a large pan over a medium heat and fry the onion and carrot for 8 minutes until soft and sweet.
Add the garlic, half the spring onions, the tomatoes and the cumin and cook for 5 minutes until jammy.
Add the beans, the stock cube and 250 ml of water, then simmer for 15 minutes, crushing a few beans with the back of a spoon to thicken the sauce.
While the beans simmer, cook the rice in boiling salted water for 10–12 minutes, drain and toss with the remaining oil and a pinch of salt.
Season the beans with salt, pepper and a squeeze of lime. Serve over the rice with avocado, the remaining spring onions, coriander and lime wedges.

recipes.title: Argentine-style chimichurri chicken with crispy potatoes
recipes.blurb: Pan-roasted chicken thighs with golden baby potatoes, charred green beans and a punchy parsley chimichurri.
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Toss the potatoes on a tray with 15 ml of the oil and a good pinch of salt and roast for 30–35 minutes, turning once, until crisp and golden.

Season the chicken with salt and pepper. Heat 15 ml of the oil in an ovenproof pan over a medium-high heat and cook skin-side down for 6–7 minutes until deep golden, then flip and roast alongside the potatoes for 12–15 minutes until cooked through.
For the chimichurri, stir together the parsley, oregano, garlic, chilli, vinegar, 30 ml of the oil and a pinch of salt in a bowl. Leave it to sit and mellow.
Boil the green beans in salted water for 3–4 minutes until just tender, drain, then toss in the remaining oil and char for 2 minutes in a hot pan.
Rest the chicken for 3 minutes, slice and serve over the potatoes with the green beans and a generous spoonful of chimichurri.

recipes.title: Peruvian-style roast chicken with green sauce
recipes.blurb: Cumin and paprika drumsticks roasted with potatoes, with a creamy coriander and jalapeño sauce for dipping.
steps: Heat the oven to 210°C (190°C fan). In a large bowl, mix the smoked paprika, cumin, two-thirds of the garlic, soy sauce, vinegar, oil, the juice of 1 lime, salt and pepper.
Add the drumsticks and the potato wedges, turning to coat, then spread on a large tray in one layer with space between the pieces.
Roast for 40–45 minutes, turning once, until the chicken is cooked through with dark, sticky skin and the potatoes are golden.
For the green sauce, blitz the coriander, jalapeños, mayonnaise, yoghurt, the remaining garlic, the juice of half the second lime and a pinch of salt with a stick blender until smooth.
Serve the chicken and potatoes with the green sauce for dipping and the rest of the lime in wedges.

recipes.title: Brazilian-style garlicky kale, black beans and fried egg
recipes.blurb: Garlicky black beans and quick-fried greens over rice, topped with a crisp fried egg and orange wedges.

ingredients.name: Kale
ingredients.prep: stalks removed, leaves very finely shredded

steps: Cook the rice in boiling salted water for 10–12 minutes, then drain and keep warm.

Heat half the oil in a frying pan over a medium heat and fry the onion for 5 minutes until soft. Add two-thirds of the garlic and cook for 1 minute, then tip in the beans with 80 ml of water and mash about a third of them. Simmer for 6 minutes until thick, then season with salt and pepper.
Heat 10 ml of the remaining oil in a large pan over a high heat and fry the remaining garlic for 20 seconds, then add the kale and toss for 3–4 minutes until wilted and bright. Season with salt.
Wipe the pan, add the last of the oil and fry the eggs over a medium-high heat for 2–3 minutes until the edges are crisp and the yolks runny.
Serve the rice with the beans and kale, topped with a fried egg and the orange wedges for squeezing.

recipes.title: Glazed meatloaf with mashed potato and peas
recipes.blurb: A tender, sticky-topped meatloaf with buttery mash and peas, the Sunday-supper classic on a weeknight.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Mix the beef mince with the onion, garlic, panko, egg, 30 ml of the milk, the Worcestershire sauce, 15 g of the ketchup, the Dijon, thyme, 2 teaspoons of salt and the pepper, using your hands, until just combined.
Shape the mixture into a loaf about 18 cm long on a lined tray. Stir the remaining ketchup into a small bowl with a splash of water and brush half of it over the top.
Bake for 35–40 minutes, brushing with the rest of the glaze halfway, until the loaf is cooked through and the top is sticky and dark.
Meanwhile, boil the potatoes in well-salted water for 15–18 minutes until completely tender. Drain well, then mash with the butter, the remaining 50 ml of milk and a pinch of salt and pepper.
Cook the peas in boiling water for 3 minutes and drain. Rest the meatloaf for 5 minutes, slice thickly and serve with the mash and peas.

recipes.title: Sloppy joes with cheddar and gherkins
recipes.blurb: Sweet, tangy, saucy beef piled into soft buns, messy in exactly the right way.
steps: Heat the oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat and brown the beef mince for 5 minutes, breaking it up, until no pink remains. Season with salt and pepper.
Add the onion and green pepper and cook for 5 minutes until softened, then stir in the garlic, tomato puree, smoked paprika and brown sugar for 1 minute.
Pour in the passata, ketchup, Worcestershire sauce, Dijon and a splash of water. Simmer for 8–10 minutes until thick and glossy but still saucy.
Toast the buns cut-side down in a dry pan or under the grill for 1–2 minutes.
Spoon the beef into the buns, scatter over the cheddar so it melts in the heat, and top with the gherkins.

recipes.title: Chicken and sausage jambalaya
recipes.blurb: Smoky, one-pot Louisiana rice with chicken, sausage and the holy trinity of onion, pepper and celery.
steps: Heat the oil in a large lidded pan over medium-high heat. Season the chicken with half the Cajun spice and a pinch of salt, then brown for 5 minutes. Add the chorizo and fry for 2 minutes until it releases its red oil.
Lower the heat to medium and add the onion, green pepper and celery. Cook for 6 minutes until softened, then stir in the garlic, tomato puree and the rest of the Cajun spice for 1 minute.
Add the rice and stir to coat in the spiced oil. Pour in the tomatoes, crumble in the stock cube and add 350 ml of water, the bay leaf and the pepper.
Bring to a simmer, cover and cook over low heat for 18 minutes without lifting the lid, until the rice is tender and has absorbed the liquid.
Rest off the heat, covered, for 5 minutes. Remove the bay leaf, fluff with a fork and serve scattered with the spring onions and parsley, with the hot sauce at the table.

recipes.title: Shrimp and cheesy grits with bacon
recipes.blurb: Creamy cheddar polenta topped with Cajun-spiced prawns and crisp bacon, a Southern supper in half an hour.
steps: Fry the bacon in a large frying pan over medium heat for 6–8 minutes until crisp. Lift out onto kitchen paper, leaving the fat in the pan.

Meanwhile, bring the milk, 400 ml of water and a good pinch of salt to a gentle boil in a saucepan. Whisk in the polenta in a steady stream and cook over low heat for 8–10 minutes, stirring often, until thick and creamy.

Toss the prawns with the Cajun spice and pepper. Add them to the bacon fat over medium-high heat with half the spring onions and cook for 2 minutes per side until pink, adding the garlic for the last 30 seconds.
Take the polenta off the heat and stir in the butter and cheddar until melted. Loosen with a splash of water if it is too stiff and season to taste.
Spoon the cheesy polenta into bowls, top with the prawns, bacon, remaining spring onions, a squeeze of lemon and the hot sauce.

recipes.title: Buttermilk oven-fried drumsticks with slaw
recipes.blurb: Buttermilk-soaked drumsticks with a crunchy panko crust, baked not fried, with a cool, tangy slaw.
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Mix 150 ml of the buttermilk with the garlic, half the paprika, 2 teaspoons of salt and the pepper in a bowl. Add the drumsticks, turn to coat and leave for at least 10 minutes.
Mix the panko with the remaining paprika and the oil on a plate. Lift each drumstick out of the buttermilk, let the excess drip off, and roll it in the crumbs, pressing so they stick.
Arrange the drumsticks on a rack set over a tray, or directly on a lined tray, and bake for 40–45 minutes, turning once, until deep golden and the juices run clear.

For the slaw, whisk the remaining 40 ml of buttermilk with the mayonnaise, the juice of half the lemon, the sugar, hot sauce and a pinch of salt. Toss with the cabbage and carrot and chill until needed.
Serve the drumsticks hot with the slaw and the remaining lemon cut into wedges.

recipes.title: Buffalo cauliflower with wedges and blue cheese dip
recipes.blurb: Crisp-battered cauliflower tossed in hot, buttery buffalo sauce with a cooling sour cream and blue cheese dip.
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Toss the potato wedges with half the oil, a good pinch of salt and the pepper on a large tray and roast for 15 minutes.

Whisk the flour, paprika, 60 ml of water and a pinch of salt into a thick batter. Coat the cauliflower in it, then add to a second oiled tray with the remaining oil, turn the wedges, and roast both for 25 minutes until the cauliflower is crisp and golden.
Meanwhile, mash the blue cheese into the sour cream with the chives, garlic, a squeeze of lemon juice and a pinch of salt for the dip. Cut the rest of the lemon into wedges.
Melt the butter in a large bowl in the oven for a minute or in a small pan, then stir in the hot sauce. Toss the hot cauliflower through it until glossy.
Serve the cauliflower with the wedges, celery and carrot sticks and the dip alongside.

recipes.title: Philly-style steak and cheese sub
recipes.blurb: Thinly sliced steak with soft onions, peppers and mushrooms, melted cheese and a toasted roll.
steps: Heat half the oil in a large frying pan over medium heat and cook the onion and green pepper for 8 minutes until soft and lightly golden. Add the mushrooms and cook for 4 minutes more, then stir in the garlic and tip everything onto a plate.
Turn the heat up to high and add the remaining oil. Fry the beef in a single layer for 1–2 minutes, turning once, seasoning with salt and pepper, until just browned.
Return the vegetables to the pan with the Worcestershire sauce, toss for 30 seconds and divide into 2 heaps, then lay the cheese over each and cover the pan for 1 minute until melted.
Toast the split baguette under the grill for 1–2 minutes and spread the cut sides with mayonnaise.
Scoop a cheesy heap of steak into each roll and serve straight away.

recipes.title: Turkey and two-bean chili with sour cream
recipes.blurb: A thick, smoky weeknight chili with lean turkey, beans and all the toppings, scooped up with tortilla chips.
steps: Heat the oil in a large pan over medium-high heat and brown the turkey mince for 6 minutes, breaking it up, until golden. Season with salt and pepper.
Add the onion and red pepper and cook for 5 minutes until softened. Stir in the garlic, chili powder, cumin, smoked paprika and oregano and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in the tomatoes and 200 ml of water, then add both beans. Bring to a simmer and cook, partly covered, for 20 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick and rich.
Squeeze in half the lime juice and season to taste. Cut the remaining lime into wedges.
Ladle into bowls and top with sour cream, cheddar, spring onions and coriander, with the tortilla chips and lime wedges on the side.

recipes.title: Black bean and avocado stuffed sweet potatoes
recipes.blurb: Fluffy baked sweet potatoes piled with smoky black beans, corn and creamy avocado lime salsa.
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Prick the sweet potatoes all over with a fork, rub with a little of the oil and salt, and bake directly on the rack for 45–50 minutes until soft right through.

Heat the remaining oil in a frying pan over medium heat and cook half the red onion for 3 minutes. Add the smoked paprika and cumin, then the black beans and sweetcorn, and cook for 5 minutes, mashing a few beans, until hot and thick.
Mix the avocado with the rest of the red onion, the juice of the lime, most of the coriander, the hot sauce and a pinch of salt and pepper.
Split the sweet potatoes lengthways and fluff the flesh with a fork. Spoon over the beans, top with the avocado salsa and finish with the remaining coriander.

recipes.title: Sticky BBQ chicken buns with crunchy slaw
recipes.blurb: Sliced chicken glazed in smoky barbecue sauce, piled into soft buns with a sharp, crunchy slaw.
steps: Mix the cabbage, carrot and spring onions with the mayonnaise, the juice of half the lemon and a pinch of salt and pepper. Chill until needed.
Toss the chicken with the smoked paprika, garlic, salt and pepper. Heat the oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat and cook for 6–7 minutes, turning, until golden and cooked through.
Pour in the barbecue sauce and a splash of water and bubble for 2 minutes, stirring, until the chicken is thickly glazed.
Toast the buns cut-side down in a dry pan for 1–2 minutes.
Fill the buns with the sticky chicken and plenty of slaw, with the remaining lemon cut into wedges on the side.

recipes.title: Smoky bean and okra gumbo with rice
recipes.blurb: A dark roux gumbo of beans, okra, peppers and celery, spiced with Cajun seasoning and ladled over fluffy rice.
steps: Make the roux: heat the oil in a large heavy pan over medium heat, whisk in the flour and cook for 8–10 minutes, stirring constantly, until it turns the colour of milk chocolate. Do not let it burn.
Add the onion, celery and green pepper straight into the roux and cook for 6 minutes, stirring, until softened. Stir in the garlic, Cajun spice, smoked paprika and thyme for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, kidney beans, crumbled stock cube, bay leaf and 500 ml of water, stirring well to dissolve the roux. Simmer, partly covered, for 20 minutes.
Meanwhile, cook the rice in boiling salted water for 11–12 minutes until tender, then drain.
Stir the okra into the gumbo for the last 10 minutes, so it softens and thickens the stew. Season, remove the bay leaf and spoon over the rice, topped with spring onions, parsley and the hot sauce.

recipes.title: Double smash burgers with special sauce and fries
recipes.blurb: Thin, lacy-edged patties smashed on a hot pan with melting cheese, pickles and a tangy burger sauce.
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Toss the potatoes with 20 ml of the oil and 1 teaspoon of salt on a large tray and roast for 30–35 minutes, turning once, until crisp.
Stir the mayonnaise, ketchup, Dijon and the chopped gherkin with the diced onion to make the sauce, and season with a little pepper.
Divide the beef mince into 4 loose balls, without squeezing them. Heat a large heavy frying pan over high heat with the remaining oil until smoking.

Add 2 balls and smash each flat with a sturdy spatula, pressing hard for 10 seconds. Season with salt and pepper, cook for 2 minutes until the edges are lacy and brown, then scrape up, flip, lay on the cheese and cook for 30 seconds. Repeat with the rest, and fry the sliced onion in the same pan for 3 minutes.
Toast the buns in the pan, spread with sauce, and build with a patty, onion, a second patty, gherkins, lettuce and tomato. Serve with the fries.

recipes.title: Chicken, bacon and avocado Cobb salad
recipes.blurb: Rows of chicken, crisp bacon, egg, avocado, tomato and blue cheese over crisp lettuce with a sharp mustard vinaigrette.
steps: Boil the eggs for 8 minutes, cool under cold running water, then peel and cut into quarters.
Meanwhile, rub the chicken with 1 tablespoon of the oil, salt and pepper. Cook in a hot frying pan for 6–7 minutes per side until golden and cooked through, then rest for 5 minutes and slice.
Fry the bacon in a separate pan over medium heat for 6–8 minutes until crisp, drain on kitchen paper and crumble.
Whisk the vinegar and Dijon with the remaining oil and a pinch of salt and pepper to make the dressing.
Spread the lettuce and leaves over plates and arrange the chicken, bacon, egg, avocado, tomatoes and blue cheese in rows. Drizzle with the dressing and scatter over the chives.

recipes.title: Mac and cheese with broccoli and spinach
recipes.blurb: Silky cheddar sauce clinging to pasta, with broccoli and spinach folded through and a crisp golden crumb.
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Boil the pasta in well-salted water for 2 minutes less than the packet says, adding the broccoli for the last 3 minutes. Drain and return to the pan with the spinach so it wilts.
Melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat, stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute. Add the milk a little at a time, whisking, then simmer for 4–5 minutes until it coats the back of a spoon.
Take off the heat and stir in 130 g of the cheddar, the Dijon and a good pinch of salt and pepper until smooth.
Fold the sauce through the pasta and vegetables and tip into a baking dish. Mix the rest of the cheddar with the panko and paprika and scatter over the top.
Bake for 12–15 minutes until bubbling at the edges and golden on top.

recipes.title: Tex-Mex black bean and rice skillet
recipes.blurb: Spiced rice, black beans, corn and peppers cooked in one pan under melting cheddar with a lime sour cream.
steps: Heat the oil in a large lidded frying pan over medium heat and cook the onion and red pepper for 6 minutes until soft. Stir in the garlic, chili powder, cumin and smoked paprika for 1 minute.
Add the rice and stir to coat, then pour in the tomatoes, crumbled stock cube and 300 ml of water. Season, bring to a simmer, cover and cook over low heat for 12 minutes.
Stir in the black beans and sweetcorn, re-cover and cook for 6 minutes more until the rice is tender.
Scatter over the cheddar and jalapeños, cover and leave for 2 minutes until melted.
Stir the sour cream with the juice of half the lime and a pinch of salt. Serve the skillet topped with the lime sour cream, coriander and the remaining lime in wedges.

recipes.title: Grilled cheese with creamy tomato soup
recipes.blurb: Golden, crisp-edged cheddar sandwiches for dunking into a velvety tomato and basil soup.
steps: Heat the oil in a saucepan over medium heat and cook the onion for 6 minutes until soft. Add the garlic and tomato puree and stir for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, crumbled stock cube, 200 ml of water, the sugar, salt and pepper. Simmer for 12 minutes, then blend until smooth and stir in the cream and half the basil.
Butter one side of each slice of bread and spread the other sides lightly with Dijon. Pile the cheddar over half the bread slices, Dijon-side up, and top with the others, butter-side out.
Fry the sandwiches in a large frying pan over medium-low heat for 3–4 minutes per side, pressing gently, until deep golden and the cheese has melted.
Cut the sandwiches in half and serve with the hot soup topped with the remaining basil.

recipes.title: Creamy corn and potato chowder
recipes.blurb: A thick, sweet and smoky chowder of corn and potato with cheddar and chives, made for tearing bread into.
steps: Melt the butter in a large pan over medium heat and cook the onion and celery for 6 minutes until soft. Stir in the garlic, smoked paprika and thyme for 1 minute.
Stir in the flour for 1 minute, then gradually pour in the milk and 300 ml of water, stirring, and crumble in the stock cube.
Add the potatoes and half the sweetcorn, bring to a simmer and cook for 15 minutes until the potato is tender.
Blend roughly a third of the chowder with a stick blender, leaving it chunky, then stir in the remaining sweetcorn and heat for 3 minutes. Season well.
Ladle into bowls and top with the cheddar and chives, with the toast alongside.

recipes.title: Smoky lentil sloppy joes on toast
recipes.blurb: Tender green lentils simmered in a sticky, smoky tomato sauce and heaped onto thick toast.
steps: Rinse the lentils and simmer in plenty of water for 20–25 minutes until tender but not mushy. Drain.
Meanwhile, heat the oil in a large frying pan over medium heat and cook the onion and green pepper for 8 minutes until soft. Stir in the garlic, tomato puree and smoked paprika for 1 minute.
Add the drained lentils with the passata, ketchup, soy sauce, brown sugar, Dijon, pepper and 100 ml of water. Simmer for 8–10 minutes until thick, stirring and mashing a few of the lentils.
Toast the bread until deep golden.
Pile the lentils onto the toast, two slices per person, and top with the gherkins.

recipes.title: Maple-mustard salmon with potatoes and green beans
recipes.blurb: Salmon roasted under a sticky maple and wholegrain mustard glaze with crisp potatoes and buttery green beans.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Toss the potatoes with the oil, a good pinch of salt and the pepper on a large tray and roast for 20 minutes.
Stir the maple syrup, wholegrain mustard and a squeeze of lemon juice together in a bowl.
Push the potatoes to one side, add the salmon skin-side down and spoon over the glaze. Roast for 10–12 minutes until the salmon is just cooked and the glaze is bubbling.
Meanwhile, boil the green beans in salted water for 4 minutes, drain and toss with the butter and a pinch of salt.
Serve the salmon with the potatoes and beans, with the remaining lemon cut into wedges.

recipes.title: Tourtière-style spiced pork pie
recipes.blurb: A Québécois Christmas-table favourite made weeknight-friendly: warmly spiced pork and potato under golden puff pastry.

ingredients.name: White potatoes
ingredients.prep: peeled and cut into small cubes

steps: Heat the oil in a large pan over medium heat and cook the onion and carrot for 6 minutes. Add the pork mince and cook for 6 minutes, breaking it up, until no pink remains.

Stir in the garlic, cinnamon, allspice, thyme, salt and pepper for 1 minute. Add the potato, crumble in the stock cube and pour in 150 ml of water. Simmer, covered, for 15 minutes until the potato is tender and most of the liquid has gone, then cool for 10 minutes.

Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Cut the pastry into two pieces, one slightly larger, and roll them a little thinner. Line a pie dish about 18 cm wide with the larger piece, leaving the edge overhanging.
Fill with the pork mixture, brush the rim with egg and cover with the second piece. Crimp the edges, brush the top with egg and cut a steam hole.
Bake for 25–30 minutes until puffed and deep golden. Boil the peas for 3 minutes and serve alongside slices of pie.

recipes.title: Québec split pea and ham soup
recipes.blurb: A thick, comforting soupe aux pois of yellow split peas and smoky ham, simmered until it falls apart.
steps: Melt the butter in a large pan over medium heat and cook the onion, carrot and celery for 8 minutes until softened. Add the garlic and thyme for 1 minute.

Add the split peas, bay leaf, crumbled stock cube, pepper and 1200 ml of water. Bring to the boil, skimming off any foam, then simmer gently for 45–50 minutes, stirring now and then, until the peas have collapsed and the soup is thick.
Stir in the ham and simmer for 5 minutes. Remove the bay leaf, add water if you want it thinner, and season with pepper, tasting before adding any salt as the ham is salty.
Ladle into bowls and serve with the toasted bread for dunking.

recipes.title: Poutine-style loaded fries with mushroom gravy
recipes.blurb: Crisp oven fries under rich mushroom gravy and squeaky, melting mozzarella standing in for the cheese curds.
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Toss the potatoes with the oil and 2 teaspoons of salt on two trays and roast for 35–40 minutes, turning and swapping the trays halfway, until golden and crisp.
Meanwhile, melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat and cook the mushrooms for 6 minutes until golden. Stir in the flour for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in 300 ml of water, then crumble in the stock cube, and add the soy sauce and pepper. Simmer for 6–8 minutes until the gravy coats the back of a spoon, and season to taste.
Pile the hot fries into bowls and scatter over the mozzarella so it starts to soften.
Pour the boiling gravy over the top so the cheese melts, and finish with the spring onions. Eat immediately, while the fries still have crunch.

recipes.title: Maple-glazed pork chops with apple and sweet potato mash
recipes.blurb: Pan-seared pork chops in a maple and mustard glaze with caramelised apple, sweet potato mash and green beans.
steps: Boil the sweet potato in salted water for 15 minutes until tender. Drain, then mash with half the butter, a squeeze of lemon juice, salt and pepper, and keep warm.
Stir the maple syrup, Dijon and thyme together. Pat the pork dry and season with salt and pepper.

Heat the oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat and sear the chops for 4 minutes per side. Add the apple and the remaining butter for the last 3 minutes, with the garlic for the final 30 seconds.
Pour the maple glaze into the pan, turn the chops to coat and bubble for 1–2 minutes until sticky. Rest the chops for 3 minutes.
Meanwhile, boil the green beans in salted water for 4 minutes and drain. Serve the chops with the apple, mash and beans, spooning over the pan glaze.

recipes.title: West Coast salmon rice bowl with avocado and edamame
recipes.blurb: Maple-soy glazed salmon over rice with avocado, cucumber, edamame and a sriracha mayo drizzle.
steps: Cook the rice in plenty of boiling water for 11–12 minutes, adding the edamame for the last 3 minutes. Drain, return to the pan and cover to keep warm.
Mix the soy sauce, maple syrup, ginger, garlic and sesame oil in a shallow dish. Add the salmon and turn it over in the marinade for 5 minutes.

Heat the vegetable oil in a non-stick frying pan over medium-high heat. Cook the salmon, skin-side down first, for 3–4 minutes per side, pouring in the remaining marinade for the last minute to glaze.
Toss the cucumber with the rice vinegar. Stir the mayonnaise and sriracha together with a splash of water until pourable.
Divide the rice and edamame between bowls and top with the salmon, cucumber, avocado and spring onions. Drizzle with the sriracha mayo and scatter with the sesame seeds.

recipes.title: Maple-roasted squash, lentil and kale bowl
recipes.blurb: Caramelised maple squash with earthy lentils, wilted kale, toasted walnuts and a sharp mustard dressing.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Toss the squash and red onion with 30 ml of the oil, the thyme, 15 ml of the maple syrup, salt and pepper on a large tray. Roast for 30–35 minutes, turning once, until soft and caramelised.
Meanwhile, simmer the lentils in plenty of water for 20–25 minutes until tender, then drain.
Whisk the wholegrain mustard, balsamic, garlic, remaining maple syrup and remaining oil with a pinch of salt for the dressing.
Toss the kale with a pinch of salt in a bowl and massage for 1 minute, then stir through the hot lentils so it wilts slightly. Add half the dressing.
Divide the lentils and kale between bowls, top with the squash and onion and scatter with the walnuts. Drizzle over the remaining dressing.

recipes.title: Thai massaman chicken curry with potatoes
recipes.blurb: Sweet, mellow and nutty, with tender chicken, soft potato and a tamarind tang over jasmine rice.

ingredients.name: White potatoes
ingredients.prep: peeled and cut into 3 cm chunks

steps: Heat the oil in a wide pan over a medium heat and fry the onion wedges for 4 minutes until they start to colour. Stir in the massaman paste and star anise and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the chicken and turn it in the paste for 2 minutes, then pour in the coconut milk and 150 ml of water. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Add the potato, tamarind, fish sauce and sugar. Simmer, partly covered, for 20–25 minutes, stirring now and then, until the potato is soft and the sauce has thickened and glossy.
Meanwhile, rinse the rice, then simmer it covered in 300 ml of water with the salt for 12 minutes. Turn off the heat and leave it covered for 5 minutes.
Toast the peanuts in a dry pan for 2–3 minutes until golden, then roughly crush them.
Taste the curry and add a splash more fish sauce or a pinch more sugar if it needs it. Spoon it over the rice and top with the peanuts and coriander.

recipes.title: Holy basil chicken with a crispy fried egg
recipes.blurb: Fiery minced chicken wok-fried with garlic and basil, piled on rice under a lacy-edged fried egg.
steps: Rinse the rice and simmer it covered in 300 ml of water with the salt for 12 minutes. Turn off the heat and leave it covered.
Mix the soy sauce, oyster sauce, fish sauce and sugar with 30 ml of water in a small bowl.

Heat 15 ml of the oil in a wok or large frying pan over a high heat. Add the garlic and chilli and stir-fry for 20 seconds, then add the chicken and break it up. Fry hard for 4–5 minutes until golden in places and cooked through.
Add the green beans and the sauce and stir-fry for 2 minutes until the beans are just tender and the sauce clings. Take off the heat and stir through most of the basil until it wilts.
Wipe out the pan, heat the remaining oil over a high heat and fry the eggs for 2 minutes until the whites are crisp and bubbly at the edges with the yolks still runny.
Spoon the rice into bowls, top with the chicken and a fried egg, and scatter over the remaining basil.

recipes.title: Larb-style pork in lettuce cups
recipes.blurb: Zingy minced pork with lime, mint and toasted rice powder, scooped up in crisp little gem leaves.
steps: Toast the rice in a dry frying pan over a medium heat for 5–6 minutes, shaking often, until deep golden. Tip it into a mortar or bowl and crush it to a coarse powder with a pestle or the base of a rolling pin.
Heat the oil in the same pan over a high heat. Add the pork and fry for 6–7 minutes, breaking it up, until cooked through and lightly browned.
Take the pan off the heat. Stir in the juice of 1½ limes, the fish sauce, sugar and chilli flakes, then fold in the shallots, toasted rice powder, mint, coriander and spring onions.
Taste and add more lime or fish sauce so it is sharp, salty and hot. Cut the remaining lime into wedges.
Pile the warm pork into the little gem leaves and serve with the lime wedges.

recipes.title: Mushroom tom kha-style coconut soup
recipes.blurb: A fragrant coconut broth with lemongrass, lime leaf and ginger, loaded with mushrooms, tofu and noodles.
steps: Heat the oil in a large saucepan over a medium heat. Fry the mushrooms for 5 minutes until they release their water and start to brown.
Add the lemongrass, ginger, lime leaves and half the chilli, and cook for 1 minute. Crumble in the stock cube, then pour in the coconut milk and 500 ml of water.
Bring to a gentle simmer and cook for 10 minutes so the aromatics flavour the broth. Do not boil hard or the coconut milk may split.
Add the tofu, soy sauce and sugar and simmer for 3 minutes. Meanwhile, soak the noodles in just-boiled water for 5 minutes, or as the packet says, then drain.
Squeeze in the juice of the lime, then taste and adjust with more soy or sugar. Divide the noodles between bowls, ladle over the soup and top with the spring onions, coriander and remaining chilli.
Leave the lemongrass, ginger and lime leaves at the side of the bowl; they flavour the soup but are not for eating.

recipes.title: Pad see ew with tofu, egg and tenderstem
recipes.blurb: Wide rice noodles charred in a hot pan with sweet soy, scrambled egg and crisp tenderstem.

ingredients.name: Firm tofu
ingredients.prep: pressed dry and cut into 2 cm cubes

steps: Soak the noodles in just-boiled water for 6–8 minutes, or as the packet says, until pliable but still firm. Drain well and toss with 15 ml of the oil so they do not stick.
Mix the soy sauce, sugar and black pepper with 30 ml of water in a small bowl.
Heat 30 ml of the oil in a large frying pan or wok over a high heat. Fry the tofu for 5 minutes, turning, until golden on most sides, then lift it onto a plate.
Add the garlic and tenderstem to the pan with a splash of water and stir-fry for 2 minutes. Push to one side, then pour the eggs into the gap and scramble for 30 seconds until just set.
Add the noodles, tofu and sauce. Toss and press the noodles against the pan for 2–3 minutes, turning, until they take on some charred spots and are coated in the sauce.
Serve straight away with the lime wedges.

recipes.title: Jungle curry-style vegetable curry
recipes.blurb: A hot, thin, coconut-free curry packed with aubergine, beans and basil, as fiery and herby as it gets.
steps: Rinse the rice and simmer it covered in 300 ml of water with the salt for 12 minutes. Turn off the heat and leave it covered.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over a medium-high heat. Fry the curry paste, lemongrass and half the chilli for 1–2 minutes, stirring, until the oil turns red and the paste smells toasted.
Add the aubergine and stir for 3 minutes, then pour in 600 ml of water, crumble in the stock cube and add the lime leaves, soy sauce and sugar.

Bring to the boil, then simmer for 8 minutes. Add the carrot and courgette and simmer for 5 minutes, then add the green beans for 4 minutes more, until everything is tender but the beans still have a bite.
Stir in most of the basil and squeeze in half the lime. Taste; it should be hot, salty and a little sweet.
Ladle into bowls over the rice, topping with the remaining basil and chilli and a wedge of the remaining lime.

recipes.title: Thai fish cakes with cucumber salad and sweet chilli dip
recipes.blurb: Bouncy, spiced white fish patties fried until golden, with a cool cucumber salad and rice.

ingredients.name: Dried lime leaves
ingredients.prep: central stems removed, very finely shredded

steps: Rinse the rice and simmer it covered in 300 ml of water with 1 g of the salt for 12 minutes. Turn off the heat and leave it covered.
Blitz the fish with the curry paste, egg, cornflour and fish sauce in a food processor until it forms a thick, sticky paste, scraping down once. Stir in the green beans and lime leaves.
Toss the cucumber with the rice vinegar, sugar and the remaining salt and leave to sit. Mix the sweet chilli sauce with a squeeze of lime juice and half the coriander.
With wet hands, shape the fish mixture into 8 flat patties about 1.5 cm thick.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan over a medium-high heat. Fry the cakes in 2 batches for 3 minutes on each side until deep golden and cooked through, then drain on kitchen paper.
Serve the fish cakes with the rice, cucumber salad and dip, sprinkled with the remaining coriander and lime wedges from the remaining lime.

recipes.title: Panang-style chicken curry
recipes.blurb: A thick, rich and lightly sweet red curry with peanut butter, lime leaf and crisp-tender peppers.
steps: Rinse the rice and simmer it covered in 300 ml of water with the salt for 12 minutes. Turn off the heat and leave it covered.

Spoon about a third of the coconut milk, the thick part from the top of the tin, into a wide pan over a medium heat with the oil. Fry the curry paste in it for 2 minutes, stirring, until it splits and smells fragrant.
Stir in the peanut butter, then add the chicken and cook for 3 minutes, turning, until the outside turns white.
Pour in the rest of the coconut milk, then add the fish sauce, sugar and lime leaves. Simmer gently for 8 minutes until the sauce is thick and glossy.
Add the red pepper and green beans and simmer for 4 minutes until crisp-tender and the chicken is cooked through.
Taste and balance with more fish sauce or sugar. Serve over the rice topped with the basil.

recipes.title: Khao soi-style curry noodles with crispy tofu
recipes.blurb: Silky turmeric coconut broth over egg noodles, with crisp tofu, quick pickled onion and chilli oil.

ingredients.name: Firm tofu
ingredients.prep: pressed dry and cut into 2 cm cubes

steps: Toss the red onion with the juice of half the lime and a pinch of the sugar and leave to pickle while you cook.
Heat 20 ml of the oil in a large pan over a medium-high heat and fry the tofu for 6–8 minutes, turning, until golden and crisp. Lift out onto a plate.
Add the remaining oil to the pan with the curry paste, curry powder, turmeric, ginger and garlic. Fry for 1–2 minutes over a medium heat, stirring, until fragrant.
Pour in the coconut milk and 300 ml of water, crumble in the stock cube and add the soy sauce and the rest of the sugar. Simmer for 10 minutes until slightly thickened.
Meanwhile, cook the noodles in boiling water for 3–4 minutes, or as the packet says, then drain well.
Divide the noodles between bowls, ladle over the broth and top with the tofu, pickled onion, spring onions, coriander and a drizzle of chilli oil. Serve with wedges of the remaining lime.

recipes.title: Thai cashew chicken stir-fry
recipes.blurb: Glossy, savoury-sweet chicken with toasted cashews, peppers and spring onions, ready in 25 minutes.
steps: Rinse the rice and simmer it covered in 300 ml of water with the salt for 12 minutes. Turn off the heat and leave it covered.
Toss the chicken with the cornflour. Mix the oyster sauce, soy sauce, sugar and chilli flakes with 60 ml of water.
Toast the cashews in a dry wok or large frying pan over a medium heat for 2–3 minutes until golden, then tip them out.
Heat the oil in the pan over a high heat. Fry the chicken for 4 minutes, turning, until golden. Add the onion, red pepper, garlic and ginger and stir-fry for 3 minutes.
Pour in the sauce and bubble for 1–2 minutes until it thickens and coats everything, then stir in the cashews and spring onions.
Serve straight away over the rice.

recipes.title: Crispy tofu and green bean red curry
recipes.blurb: Golden cornflour-crusted tofu and snappy beans in a creamy, chilli-warm red coconut sauce.

ingredients.name: Firm tofu
ingredients.prep: pressed dry and cut into 2 cm cubes

steps: Rinse the rice and simmer it covered in 300 ml of water with 1 g of the salt for 12 minutes. Turn off the heat and leave it covered.

Toss the tofu with the cornflour and the rest of the salt until evenly coated. Heat 30 ml of the oil in a large frying pan over a medium-high heat and fry the tofu for 8 minutes, turning, until golden and crisp. Lift out onto a plate.
In a wide pan, heat the remaining oil over a medium heat and fry the curry paste for 1–2 minutes until fragrant. Pour in the coconut milk and add the lime leaves, soy sauce and sugar.
Simmer for 5 minutes, then add the green beans and red pepper and cook for 5–6 minutes until just tender.
Fold the crispy tofu into the sauce, squeeze in half the lime and taste for balance. Serve over the rice with the basil and wedges from the remaining lime.

recipes.title: Thai prawn fried rice with egg and lime
recipes.blurb: Wok-hot rice with juicy prawns, egg and garlic, finished with cool cucumber, tomato and lime.
steps: Rinse the rice and simmer it covered in 300 ml of water with the salt for 12 minutes. Spread it on a tray and leave to cool and dry out for 10 minutes; cold rice fries far better than steaming-hot rice.
Mix the fish sauce, soy sauce, sugar and black pepper in a small bowl.
Heat 15 ml of the oil in a wok or large frying pan over a high heat. Fry the prawns for 2 minutes until pink, then tip them onto a plate.

Add the remaining oil and fry the onion for 2 minutes, then add the garlic, chilli and the white parts of the spring onions for 30 seconds. Push to the side, crack in the eggs and scramble for 30 seconds.
Add the rice and sauce and stir-fry hard for 3–4 minutes, breaking up any lumps. Return the prawns and toss for 1 minute.
Serve topped with the tomato, cucumber, coriander and the green parts of the spring onions, with the lime wedges for squeezing.

recipes.title: Butternut squash and chickpea Thai green curry
recipes.blurb: Sweet roast-soft squash and spinach in a fragrant green coconut curry, bulked out with chickpeas.

ingredients.name: Butternut squash
ingredients.prep: peeled and cut into 2 cm cubes

steps: Rinse the rice and simmer it covered in 300 ml of water with the salt for 12 minutes. Turn off the heat and leave it covered.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over a medium heat. Fry the green paste for 1–2 minutes, stirring, until fragrant.
Add the squash and stir to coat, then pour in the coconut milk and 150 ml of water. Add the lime leaves, soy sauce and sugar.
Simmer, partly covered, for 15 minutes, stirring now and then, until the squash is tender when pierced with a knife.
Stir in the chickpeas and cook for 3 minutes, then add the spinach and stir until wilted, about 1 minute.
Squeeze in half the lime and taste for salt, sweetness and sourness. Serve over the rice with the basil and wedges from the remaining lime.

recipes.title: Thai-style steak salad with lime, mint and chilli
recipes.blurb: Seared sliced steak tossed with crunchy cucumber, tomato and herbs in a hot, sour, salty dressing.
steps: Pat the steak dry and season both sides with the salt and black pepper.

Heat the oil in a frying pan over a high heat until almost smoking. Sear the steak for 2–3 minutes on each side for medium-rare, longer if you prefer it more done, then rest it on a board for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, whisk the juice of 2 limes with the fish sauce, sugar and half the chilli until the sugar dissolves.
Toss the cucumber, tomatoes, red onion, mint and coriander in a large bowl with most of the dressing.
Slice the steak thinly against the grain and toss it gently with the salad and the juices from the board.
Arrange the little gem leaves on plates, pile the salad on top, spoon over the remaining dressing and scatter with the remaining chilli.

recipes.title: Shaking beef with peppery lime dip and rocket
recipes.blurb: Seared garlicky beef cubes, shaken in a hot pan, with a salt-and-pepper lime dip and peppery leaves.
steps: Toss the beef with half the garlic, the soy sauce, oyster sauce, fish sauce, half the sugar and 1 g of the black pepper. Leave to marinate for 15 minutes while you cook the rice.
Rinse the rice and simmer it covered in 300 ml of water with 1 g of the salt for 12 minutes. Turn off the heat and leave it covered.
